title.raw: 卷四十七 志第二十三 禮一 Volume 47 Treatises 23: Rites 1

sentences.zh: 志第二十三 禮一

translations.literal: Treatise Twenty-three: Rites, Part One
translations.idiomatic: Treatise Twenty-three: Rites, Part One

translations.literal: Opening section bracket 〈
translations.idiomatic: Opening section bracket 〈

sentences.zh: （吉禮一）〉

translations.literal: (Auspicious Rites, Part One)〉
translations.idiomatic: (Auspicious Rites, Part One)〉

sentences.zh: 《周官》、《儀禮》尚已，然書缺簡脫，因革莫詳。

translations.literal: The 《Offices of Zhou》 and 《Ceremonial Rituals》 still survive, yet the books suffer from missing sections and lost slips, and their reforms and changes cannot be fully known.
translations.idiomatic: The 《Rites of Zhou》 and 《Etiquette and Ceremonial》 still exist, but the texts are fragmentary and incomplete, so their evolution cannot be fully traced.

sentences.zh: 自漢史作《禮志》，後皆因之，一代之制，始的然可考。

translations.literal: Since the Han histories composed the 《Treatise on Rites》, later dynasties all followed them, and only then did each dynasty's institutions become clearly ascertainable.
translations.idiomatic: After the Han histories introduced the 《Treatise on Rites》, later dynasties all followed suit, and only then did the ritual institutions of each age become reliably documented.

sentences.zh: 歐陽氏云：「三代以下，治出於二，而禮樂爲虛名。

translations.literal: Ouyang Xiu said: "After the Three Dynasties, governance issued from two sources, while rites and music became empty names."
translations.idiomatic: Ouyang Xiu remarked: "After the Three Dynasties, governance derived from two competing channels, and rites and music became little more than names."

sentences.zh: 」要其用之郊廟朝廷，下至閭里州黨者，未嘗無可觀也。

translations.literal: "Yet in their application from suburban altars and ancestral temples through the court, down to hamlets, townships, and local districts, there is never nothing worth observing."
translations.idiomatic: "Yet from suburban sacrifices and ancestral temples through the court, and on down to villages and local communities, they still offer much that is worth studying."

sentences.zh: 惟能修明講貫，以實意行乎其間，則格上下、感鬼神，教化之成即在是矣。

translations.literal: Only if one can clarify and thoroughly master them, and execute them with genuine intent, then harmonizing above and below and moving spirits and ghosts—the accomplishment of transformation and instruction lies precisely in this.
translations.idiomatic: Only when they are studied, clarified, and practiced with genuine sincerity can they unite heaven and earth, move spirits, and accomplish moral transformation.

sentences.zh: 安見後世之禮，必不可上追三代哉。

translations.literal: How can one know that the rites of later ages cannot possibly be traced upward to the Three Dynasties?
translations.idiomatic: Who is to say that the rites of later ages can never rise to match those of the Three Dynasties?

sentences.zh: 明太祖初定天下，他務未遑，首開禮、樂二局，廣徵耆儒，分曹究討。

translations.literal: When the Ming founding emperor first secured the realm, with no leisure for other affairs, he first established two bureaus for rites and music, broadly summoned elderly Confucian scholars, and assigned them to teams for thorough investigation.
translations.idiomatic: When the Hongwu Emperor first unified the realm, though pressed by other duties, he promptly established bureaus for rites and music, summoned eminent scholars from far and wide, and organized them into commissions for exhaustive study.

sentences.zh: 洪武元年，命中書省暨翰林院、太常司，定擬祀典。

translations.literal: In the first year of Hongwu, he ordered the Secretariat together with the Hanlin Academy and the Court of Imperial Sacrifices to draft the sacrificial canon.
translations.idiomatic: In Hongwu 1, he charged the Secretariat, the Hanlin Academy, and the Court of Imperial Sacrifices with drafting the state sacrificial code.

sentences.zh: 乃歷敘沿革之由，酌定郊社宗廟儀以進。

translations.literal: They then narrated in sequence the reasons for successive changes, weighed and fixed the rites for suburban altars, altars of soil and grain, and the ancestral temple, and presented them.
translations.idiomatic: They traced the historical evolution of these rites, settled the ceremonies for suburban sacrifices, the altars of soil and grain, and the ancestral temple, and submitted their recommendations.

sentences.zh: 禮官及諸儒臣又編集郊廟山川等儀，及古帝王祭祀感格可垂鑑戒者，名曰《存心錄》。

translations.literal: The ritual officials and various Confucian ministers also compiled the rites for suburban altars, temples, mountains and rivers, and cases of ancient emperors and kings whose sacrifices elicited spiritual responses worthy of emulation as warnings, naming it the 《Record of Preserving the Heart》.
translations.idiomatic: Ritual officials and scholar-ministers also compiled ceremonies for suburban altars, temples, mountains, and rivers, together with precedents of ancient rulers whose sacrifices had moved heaven—examples meant as lasting lessons—and titled the work the 《Record of Preserving the Heart》.

sentences.zh: 二年，詔諸儒臣修禮書。

translations.literal: In the second year, an edict ordered the Confucian ministers to compile a book of rites.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year, an imperial edict directed the scholar-officials to compile a comprehensive book of rites.

sentences.zh: 明年告成，賜名《大明集禮》。

translations.literal: The next year it was reported complete and bestowed the name 《Collected Rites of the Great Ming》.
translations.idiomatic: The following year the work was completed and given the title 《Collected Rites of the Great Ming》.

sentences.zh: 其書準五禮而益以冠服、車輅、儀仗、鹵簿、字學、音樂，凡升降儀節，制度名數，纖悉畢具。

translations.literal: The book took the five rites as its standard and added caps and robes, chariots and carriages, ceremonial regalia, imperial escort arrays, philology, and music; every ascending and descending ceremonial detail, institutional title and number, was minutely and completely provided.
translations.idiomatic: The work followed the five categories of rites and added sections on caps and robes, chariots, ceremonial regalia, imperial processions, philology, and music, setting forth every detail of ceremonial movement, institutional nomenclature, and numerical specification in exhaustive completeness.

sentences.zh: 又屢敕議禮臣李善長、傅瓛、宋濂、詹同、陶安、劉基、魏觀、崔亮、牛諒、陶凱、硃升、樂韶鳳、李原名等，編輯成集。

translations.literal: He also repeatedly ordered the ritual deliberators Li Shanchang, Fu Yong, Song Lian, Zhan Tong, Tao An, Liu Ji, Wei Guan, Cui Liang, Niu Liang, Tao Kai, Zhu Sheng, Yue Shaofeng, Li Yuanming, and others to compile and complete collections.
translations.idiomatic: He also repeatedly directed the ritual deliberators Li Shanchang, Fu Yong, Song Lian, Zhan Tong, Tao An, Liu Ji, Wei Guan, Cui Liang, Niu Liang, Tao Kai, Zhu Sheng, Yue Shaofeng, Li Yuanming, and others to compile and complete these collections.

sentences.zh: 且詔郡縣舉高潔博雅之士徐一夔、樑寅、周子諒、胡行簡、劉宗弼、董彝、蔡深、滕公琰至京，同修禮書。

translations.literal: Moreover he ordered the commanderies and counties to recommend men of lofty integrity and broad learning—Xu Yikui, Liang Yin, Zhou Ziliang, Hu Xingjian, Liu Zongbi, Dong Yi, Cai Shen, Teng Gongyan—to the capital to jointly compile the book of rites.
translations.idiomatic: He also ordered local governments to recommend scholars of integrity and erudition—Xu Yikui, Liang Yin, Zhou Ziliang, Hu Xingjian, Liu Zongbi, Dong Yi, Cai Shen, and Teng Gongyan—to the capital to join in compiling the ritual codes.

sentences.zh: 在位三十餘年，所著書可考見者，曰《孝慈錄》，曰《洪武禮制》，曰《禮儀定式》，曰《諸司職掌》，曰《稽古定制》，曰《國朝製作》，曰《大禮要議》，曰《皇朝禮制》，曰《大明禮制》，曰《洪武禮法》，曰《禮制集要》，曰《禮制節文》，曰《太常集禮》，曰《禮書》。

translations.literal: During more than thirty years on the throne, the works he authored that can be verified include: the 《Record of Filial Piety and Compassion》, the 《Hongwu Ritual System》, the 《Fixed Forms of Ritual Etiquette》, the 《Duties of the Various Offices》, the 《Ancient Models for Reference》, the 《Institutions of the Dynasty》, the 《Essential Deliberations on Major Rites》, the 《Ritual System of the Imperial Court》, the 《Ritual System of the Great Ming》, the 《Hongwu Ritual Laws》, the 《Collected Essentials of the Ritual System》, the 《Abridged Texts of the Ritual System》, the 《Collected Rites of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices》, and the 《Book of Rites》.
translations.idiomatic: Over more than thirty years on the throne, the ritual works attributable to his reign include the 《Record of Filial Piety and Compassion》, the 《Hongwu Ritual System》, the 《Fixed Forms of Ritual Etiquette》, the 《Duties of the Various Offices》, the 《Ancient Models for Reference》, the 《Institutions of the Dynasty》, the 《Essential Deliberations on Major Rites》, the 《Ritual System of the Imperial Court》, the 《Ritual System of the Great Ming》, the 《Hongwu Ritual Laws》, the 《Collected Essentials of the Ritual System》, the 《Abridged Texts of the Ritual System》, the 《Collected Rites of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices》, and the 《Book of Rites》.

sentences.zh: 若夫釐正祀典，凡天皇、太乙、六天、五帝之類，皆爲革除，而諸神封號，悉改從本稱，一洗矯誣陋習，其度越漢、唐遠矣。

translations.literal: As for rectifying the sacrificial canon, all such categories as the Heavenly Emperor, the Great Unity, the Six Heavens, and the Five Emperors were abolished, and the enfeoffed titles of the various spirits were all changed to follow their original designations, thoroughly washing away perverse, false, and vulgar customs—his surpassing of Han and Tang was far indeed.
translations.idiomatic: In rectifying the sacrificial canon, he abolished such cults as the Heavenly Emperor, the Great Unity, the Six Heavens, and the Five Emperors, restored the original names of the various deities, and swept away centuries of spurious and vulgar practice—an achievement that far surpassed the Han and Tang.

sentences.zh: 又詔定國恤，父母並斬衰，長子降爲期年，正服旁服以遞而殺，斟酌古今，蓋得其中。

translations.literal: He also ordered the fixing of state mourning: for both parents, the highest grade of mourning garment; the eldest son reduced to one year; principal and collateral mourning garments diminishing in succession—weighing ancient and modern, he broadly attained the mean.
translations.idiomatic: He also standardized state mourning regulations: both parents received the highest grade of mourning dress, the eldest son's mourning was reduced to one year, and principal and collateral mourning garments were scaled down in succession—a balanced synthesis of ancient and modern practice.

sentences.zh: 永樂中，頒《文公家禮》於天下，又定巡狩、監國及經筵日講之制。

translations.literal: During the Yongle reign, the 《Family Rites of Master Zhu》 was promulgated throughout the realm, and the systems for imperial tours of inspection, regency, and daily lectures at the Classics Colloquium were also fixed.
translations.idiomatic: During the Yongle reign, the 《Family Rites of Master Zhu》 was promulgated empire-wide, and regulations were established for imperial tours, regency, and daily lectures at the Classics Colloquium.

sentences.zh: 後宮罷殉，始於英宗。

translations.literal: The abolition of consort sacrifice in the inner palace began with Emperor Yingzong.
translations.idiomatic: The abolition of consort burial sacrifice in the inner palace began under Emperor Yingzong.

sentences.zh: 陵廟嫡庶之分，正於孝宗。

translations.literal: The distinction between legitimate and secondary lines in imperial tombs and temples was rectified under Emperor Xiaozong.
translations.idiomatic: The proper distinction between legitimate and secondary heirs in imperial tombs and ancestral temples was established under Emperor Xiaozong.

sentences.zh: 暨乎世宗，以制禮作樂自任。

translations.literal: By the time of Emperor Shizong, he took upon himself the task of establishing rites and composing music.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Shizong came to the throne, he took personal charge of reforming rites and composing music.

sentences.zh: 其更定之大者，如分祀天地，復朝日夕月於東西郊，罷二祖並配，以及祈谷大雩，享先蠶，祭聖師，易至聖先師號，皆能折衷於古。

translations.literal: Among his major revisions were such matters as separating the sacrifices to Heaven and Earth, restoring the worship of the rising sun and setting moon at the eastern and western suburbs, abolishing the joint enshrinement of the two founding ancestors, as well as the prayers for grain and the great rain sacrifice, offerings to the Sericulture Ancestress, sacrifices to the Sage Master, and changing the title to Most Sage and First Teacher—all able to strike a balance with antiquity.
translations.idiomatic: His major reforms—separating the sacrifices to Heaven and Earth, restoring the worship of the sun and moon at the eastern and western suburbs, ending the joint enshrinement of the two founding ancestors, and revising the prayers for grain, the great rain sacrifice, offerings to the Sericulture Ancestress, sacrifices to Confucius, and the title Most Sage and First Teacher—generally struck a sound balance with ancient precedent.

sentences.zh: 獨其排衆議，祔睿宗太廟躋武宗上，徇本生而違大統，以明察始而以豐暱終矣。

translations.literal: Only in rejecting the consensus of opinion, enshrining Emperor Ruizong in the Grand Ancestral Temple and placing him above Emperor Wuzong, indulging his biological father while violating the great succession—from perspicacity at the start to excessive favoritism at the end.
translations.idiomatic: Yet in overruling court opinion to enshrine his father Ruizong in the Grand Ancestral Temple above Emperor Wuzong, he favored his biological parent at the expense of dynastic succession—beginning with keen judgment and ending in excessive partiality.

sentences.zh: 當時將順之臣，各爲之說。

translations.literal: The compliant ministers of that time each devised arguments for him.
translations.idiomatic: The courtiers who accommodated his wishes each devised their own justifications.

sentences.zh: 今其存者，若《明倫大典》，則御製序文以行之；

translations.literal: Of those that survive today, such as the 《Great Canon of Clarifying Human Relations》, an imperially composed preface was written to promulgate it;
translations.idiomatic: Among those that survive today, the 《Great Canon of Clarifying Human Relations》 was promulgated with an imperial preface;

sentences.zh: 《祀儀成典》，則李時等奉敕而修；

translations.literal: the 《Completed Canon of Sacrificial Rites》 was compiled by Li Shi and others on imperial command;
translations.idiomatic: the 《Completed Canon of Sacrificial Rites》 was compiled on imperial order by Li Shi and others;

sentences.zh: 《郊祀考議》，則張孚敬所進者也。

translations.literal: the 《Deliberations on Suburban Sacrifices》 was what Zhang Fuqing presented.
translations.idiomatic: and the 《Deliberations on Suburban Sacrifices》 was submitted by Zhang Fuqing.

sentences.zh: 至《大明會典》，自孝宗朝集纂，其於禮制尤詳。

translations.literal: As for the 《Collected Statutes of the Great Ming》, compiled from the Xiaozong reign, it is especially detailed on ritual institutions.
translations.idiomatic: The 《Collected Statutes of the Great Ming》, compiled from the Xiaozong reign onward, is especially comprehensive on ritual institutions.

sentences.zh: 世宗、神宗時，數有增益，一代成憲，略具是焉。

translations.literal: During the reigns of Shizong and Shenzong there were several additions; the established institutions of the dynasty are broadly complete therein.
translations.idiomatic: Further additions were made under Emperors Shizong and Shenzong, so that the dynasty's established ritual code is largely preserved in these works.

sentences.zh: 今以五禮之序，條爲品式，而隨時損益者，則依類編入，以識沿革云。

translations.literal: Now, following the order of the five rites, items are arranged as categories and forms, while those altered with the times are entered by category to record successive changes.
translations.idiomatic: The present account follows the order of the five rites, arranging them by category and form, while changes made over time are entered under the appropriate headings to trace their evolution.

sentences.zh: 壇壝之制 神位祭器玉帛牲牢祝冊之數 籩豆之實

translations.literal: Regulations for altars and enclosures; numbers of spirit tablets, sacrificial vessels, jades and silks, sacrificial animals, and prayer documents; contents of the baskets and stands
translations.idiomatic: Regulations for altars and enclosures; spirit tablets, sacrificial vessels, jades and silks, sacrificial animals, and prayer documents; contents of the offering baskets and stands

sentences.zh: 祭祀雜議諸儀 祭祀日期 習儀 齋戒 遣官祭祀

translations.literal: Miscellaneous deliberations and various rites for sacrifices; dates of sacrifice; rehearsal of rites; purification and fasting; dispatching officials to perform sacrifices
translations.idiomatic: Miscellaneous deliberations and ceremonial details of sacrifice; dates of sacrifice; rehearsal of rites; purification and fasting; dispatching officials to perform sacrifices

sentences.zh: ○分獻陪祀

translations.literal: ○ Distributed offerings and accompanying sacrifice
translations.idiomatic: ○ Distributed offerings and accompanying sacrifice

sentences.zh: 五禮，一曰吉禮。

translations.literal: Of the five rites, the first is auspicious rites.
translations.idiomatic: Of the five categories of rites, the first is auspicious rites.

sentences.zh: 凡祀事，皆領於太常寺而屬於禮部。

translations.literal: All sacrificial affairs are directed by the Court of Imperial Sacrifices and subordinate to the Ministry of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: All sacrificial affairs were administered by the Court of Imperial Sacrifices under the Ministry of Rites.

sentences.zh: 明初以圜丘、方澤、宗廟、社稷、朝日、夕月、先農爲大祀，太歲、星辰、風雲雷雨、嶽鎮、海瀆、山川、歷代帝王、先師、旗纛、司中、司命、司民、司祿、壽星爲中祀，諸神爲小祀。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Ming, the Circular Mound, the Square Pond, the ancestral temple, the altars of soil and grain, the morning sun, the evening moon, and the Agriculture Ancestor were great sacrifices; the Grand Year Star, stars and constellations, wind, clouds, thunder, and rain, peaks and garrisons, seas and rivers, mountains and rivers, successive dynasties' emperors and kings, the First Teacher, banners and pennants, the Director of the Center, the Director of Fate, the Director of the People, the Director of Emolument, and the Longevity Star were middle sacrifices; the various spirits were minor sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the dynasty, the Circular Mound, the Square Pond, the ancestral temple, the altars of soil and grain, the morning sun, the evening moon, and the Agriculture Ancestor ranked as great sacrifices; the Grand Year Star, stars and constellations, wind, clouds, thunder, and rain, sacred peaks, seas and rivers, mountains and rivers, successive dynasties' emperors, Confucius, banners and pennants, and the spirits of the center, fate, people, emolument, and longevity ranked as middle sacrifices; and all other deities ranked as minor sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 後改先農、朝日、夕月爲中祀。

translations.literal: Later the Agriculture Ancestor, the morning sun, and the evening moon were changed to middle sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: Later the Agriculture Ancestor and the sacrifices to the morning sun and evening moon were downgraded to middle sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 凡天子所親祀者，天地、宗廟、社稷、山川。

translations.literal: What the Son of Heaven personally sacrifices to are Heaven and Earth, the ancestral temple, the altars of soil and grain, and mountains and rivers.
translations.idiomatic: The Son of Heaven personally performed sacrifices to Heaven and Earth, the ancestral temple, the altars of soil and grain, and mountains and rivers.

sentences.zh: 若國有大事，則命官祭告。

translations.literal: If the state had a great affair, officials were ordered to sacrifice and announce it.
translations.idiomatic: When the state faced a major event, officials were dispatched to offer sacrificial announcements.

sentences.zh: 其中祀小祀，皆遣官致祭，而帝王陵廟及孔子廟，則傳制特遣焉。

translations.literal: Middle and minor sacrifices were all performed by dispatched officials, while imperial tombs and temples and the temple of Confucius were specially dispatched by transmitted decree.
translations.idiomatic: Middle and minor sacrifices were performed by dispatched officials, while imperial tombs and temples and the Temple of Confucius received specially commissioned envoys by imperial decree.

sentences.zh: 每歲所常行者，大祀十有三：正月上辛祈谷、孟夏大雩、季秋大享、冬至圜丘皆祭昊天上帝，夏至方丘祭皇地祇，春分朝日於東郊，秋分夕月於西郊，四孟季冬享太廟，仲春仲秋上戊祭太社太稷。

translations.literal: What was regularly performed each year: thirteen great sacrifices—the first xin day of the first month for praying for grain, the great rain sacrifice in the first month of summer, the great offering in the last month of autumn, and the Circular Mound at the winter solstice all sacrificed to the August Supreme Lord of Heaven; the Square Mound at the summer solstice sacrificed to the August Sovereign Earth Spirit; the morning sun at the spring equinox in the eastern suburb; the evening moon at the autumn equinox in the western suburb; the Grand Ancestral Temple in all four first months and the last month of winter; the Great Altars of Soil and Grain on the first wu days of the second and eighth months.
translations.idiomatic: The thirteen great sacrifices performed annually were: on the first xin day of the first month, prayers for grain; in early summer, the great rain sacrifice; in late autumn, the great offering; and at the winter solstice, sacrifice at the Circular Mound to the Supreme Lord of Heaven; at the summer solstice, sacrifice at the Square Mound to the Sovereign Earth Spirit; at the spring equinox, the morning sun in the eastern suburb; at the autumn equinox, the evening moon in the western suburb; offerings at the Grand Ancestral Temple in all four first months and the last month of winter; and on the first wu days of the second and eighth months, sacrifice at the Great Altars of Soil and Grain.

sentences.zh: 中祀二十有五：仲春仲秋上戊之明日，祭帝社帝稷，仲秋祭太歲、風雲雷雨、四季月將及嶽鎮、海瀆、山川、城隍，霜降日祭旗纛於教場，仲秋祭城南旗纛廟，仲春祭先農，仲秋祭天神地祗于山川壇，仲春仲秋祭歷代帝王廟，春秋仲月上丁祭先師孔子。

translations.literal: Twenty-five middle sacrifices: the day after the first wu days of the second and eighth months, sacrifice to the Emperor's Altars of Soil and Grain; in mid-autumn sacrifice to the Grand Year Star, wind, clouds, thunder, and rain, the seasonal generals of the four seasons, and the peaks, garrisons, seas, rivers, mountains, rivers, and city god; on the frost-descent day sacrifice to banners and pennants at the drill ground; in mid-autumn sacrifice at the southern suburban Banner and Pennant Temple; in mid-spring sacrifice to the Agriculture Ancestor; in mid-autumn sacrifice to the spirits of Heaven and Earth at the Mountain and River Altar; in mid-spring and mid-autumn sacrifice at the Temple of Successive Dynasties' Emperors; on the first ding days of spring and autumn sacrifice to the First Teacher Confucius.
translations.idiomatic: The twenty-five middle sacrifices included: the day after the first wu days of the second and eighth months, sacrifice at the Emperor's Altars of Soil and Grain; in mid-autumn, sacrifice to the Grand Year Star, wind, clouds, thunder, and rain, the seasonal generals, sacred peaks, seas, rivers, mountains, rivers, and the city god; on the frost-descent day, sacrifice to banners and pennants at the drill ground; in mid-autumn, sacrifice at the southern suburban Banner and Pennant Temple; in mid-spring, sacrifice to the Agriculture Ancestor; in mid-autumn, sacrifice to the spirits of Heaven and Earth at the Mountain and River Altar; in mid-spring and mid-autumn, sacrifice at the Temple of Successive Dynasties' Emperors; and on the first ding days of spring and autumn, sacrifice to Confucius.

sentences.zh: 小祀八：孟春祭司戶，孟夏祭司竈，季夏祭中霤，孟秋祭司門，孟冬祭司井，仲春祭司馬之神，清明、十月朔祭泰厲，又於每月朔望祭火雷之神。

translations.literal: Eight minor sacrifices: in the first month of spring sacrifice to the Household Spirit; in the first month of summer sacrifice to the Kitchen Spirit; in the last month of summer sacrifice to the Central Drain; in the first month of autumn sacrifice to the Gate Spirit; in the first month of winter sacrifice to the Well Spirit; in the second month of spring sacrifice to the Horse Spirit; on Qingming and the first day of the tenth month sacrifice to the Great Specter; and on each new and full moon sacrifice to the spirits of fire and thunder.
translations.idiomatic: The eight minor sacrifices were: in early spring, the Household Spirit; in early summer, the Kitchen Spirit; in late summer, the Central Drain; in early autumn, the Gate Spirit; in early winter, the Well Spirit; in mid-spring, the Horse Spirit; on Qingming and the first day of the tenth month, the Great Specter; and at each new and full moon, the spirits of fire and thunder.

sentences.zh: 至京師十廟、南京十五廟，各以歲時遣官致祭。

translations.literal: As for the ten temples in the capital and fifteen temples in Nanjing, each year officials were dispatched to perform sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: At the ten temples in the capital and fifteen in Nanjing, officials were dispatched annually to perform the sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 其非常祀而間行之者，若新天子耕耤而享先農，視學而行釋奠之類。

translations.literal: Those that were irregular sacrifices performed intermittently, such as the new Son of Heaven plowing the sacred field and offering to the Agriculture Ancestor, or inspecting the schools and performing the libation sacrifice—such categories.
translations.idiomatic: Irregular sacrifices performed on special occasions included the new emperor's plowing of the sacred field and offering to the Agriculture Ancestor, and the libation sacrifice upon inspecting the schools.

sentences.zh: 嘉靖時，皇后享先蠶，祀高禖，皆因時特舉者也。

translations.literal: During the Jiajing reign, the empress offered to the Sericulture Ancestress and sacrificed to the High Consort—all were specially performed according to the occasion.
translations.idiomatic: During the Jiajing reign, the empress's offerings to the Sericulture Ancestress and sacrifices to the High Consort were likewise special observances instituted for particular occasions.

sentences.zh: 其王國所祀，則太廟、社稷、風雲雷雨、封內山川、城隍、旗纛、五祀、厲壇。

translations.literal: What the princely states sacrificed to were: the Grand Ancestral Temple, the altars of soil and grain, wind, clouds, thunder, and rain, mountains and rivers within their domains, the city god, banners and pennants, the five sacrifices, and the Specter Altar.
translations.idiomatic: Princely domains sacrificed at the Grand Ancestral Temple, the altars of soil and grain, to wind, clouds, thunder, and rain, to mountains and rivers within their territories, to the city god, banners and pennants, the five household spirits, and the Specter Altar.

sentences.zh: 府州縣所祀，則社稷、風雲雷雨、山川、厲壇、先師廟及所在帝王陵廟，各衛亦祭先師。

translations.literal: What prefectures, departments, and counties sacrificed to were: the altars of soil and grain, wind, clouds, thunder, and rain, mountains and rivers, the Specter Altar, the temple of the First Teacher, and imperial tombs and temples in their locales; each guard also sacrificed to the First Teacher.
translations.idiomatic: Prefectures, departments, and counties sacrificed at the altars of soil and grain, to wind, clouds, thunder, and rain, mountains and rivers, the Specter Altar, the Temple of Confucius, and local imperial tombs and temples; military guards also maintained sacrifices to Confucius.

sentences.zh: 至於庶人，亦得祭里社、穀神及祖父母、父母並祀竈，載在祀典。

translations.literal: As for commoners, they were also permitted to sacrifice to the local altar of soil and grain, the Grain Spirit, and their grandparents and parents, and jointly to sacrifice to the Kitchen Spirit—all recorded in the sacrificial canon.
translations.idiomatic: Commoners were also permitted to sacrifice at the local altar of soil and grain, to the Grain Spirit, to their grandparents and parents, and at the Kitchen Spirit—all as recorded in the sacrificial canon.

sentences.zh: 雖時稍有更易，其大要莫能逾也。

translations.literal: Although there were occasional changes with the times, the general principles could not be exceeded.
translations.idiomatic: Although details shifted over time, the fundamental framework remained essentially unchanged.

sentences.zh: 至若壇壝之制，神位、祭器、玉帛、牲牢、祝冊之數，籩豆之實，酒齊之名，析其彼此之異同，訂其初終之損益，臚於首簡，略於本條，庶無缺遺，亦免繁復云爾。

translations.literal: As for regulations for altars and enclosures, the numbers of spirit tablets, sacrificial vessels, jades and silks, sacrificial animals, and prayer documents, the contents of baskets and stands, and the names of fermented liquors—analyzing their mutual differences and similarities, fixing their initial and final additions and subtractions, setting them forth at the head while abbreviating in the main entries, so as to have no omissions and also avoid redundancy.
translations.idiomatic: Regulations for altars and enclosures, spirit tablets, sacrificial vessels, jades and silks, sacrificial animals, prayer documents, offering baskets and stands, and ritual wines are compared for their variations, and their successive changes are recorded at the outset while the main entries remain concise, so that nothing essential is omitted yet needless repetition is avoided.

sentences.zh: ○壇壝之制

translations.literal: ○ Regulations for altars and enclosures
translations.idiomatic: ○ Regulations for altars and enclosures

sentences.zh: 明初，建圜丘於正陽門外，鐘山之陽，方丘於太平門外，鐘山之陰。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Ming, the Circular Mound was built outside the Gate of Correct Yang, on the southern slope of Bell Mountain; the Square Mound outside the Gate of Great Peace, on the northern slope of Bell Mountain.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the dynasty, the Circular Mound was built outside the Gate of Correct Yang on the southern slope of Bell Mountain, and the Square Mound outside the Gate of Great Peace on its northern slope.

sentences.zh: 圜丘壇二成。

translations.literal: The Circular Mound altar had two tiers.
translations.idiomatic: The Circular Mound altar had two tiers.

sentences.zh: 上成廣七丈，高八尺一寸，四出陛，各九級，正南廣九尺五寸，東、西、北八尺一寸。

translations.literal: The upper tier was seven zhang wide and eight chi one cun high, with steps on four sides, each of nine steps; due south was nine chi five cun wide, east, west, and north eight chi one cun.
translations.idiomatic: The upper tier measured seven zhang across and eight chi one cun in height, with steps on all four sides of nine steps each; the southern stairway was nine chi five cun wide, and those on the east, west, and north were eight chi one cun.

sentences.zh: 下成周圍壇面，縱橫皆廣五丈，高視上成，陛皆九級，正南廣一丈二尺五寸，東、西、北殺五寸五分。

translations.literal: The lower tier's altar surface all around was five zhang wide in both length and breadth, its height matching the upper tier; the steps were all of nine steps; due south was one zhang two chi five cun wide, east, west, and north diminishing by five cun five fen.
translations.idiomatic: The lower tier's platform measured five zhang square, matching the upper tier in height, with nine-step stairways on each side; the southern stairway was one zhang two chi five cun wide, and those on the east, west, and north were five cun five fen narrower.

sentences.zh: 甃證磚闌盾，皆以琉璃爲之。

translations.literal: The paved bricks, balustrades, and parapets were all made of glazed tile.
translations.idiomatic: The paving bricks, balustrades, and parapets were all made of glazed tile.

sentences.zh: 壝去壇十五丈，高八尺一寸，四面靈星門，南三門，東、西、北各一。

translations.literal: The enclosure was fifteen zhang from the altar, eight chi one cun high, with Spirit Star gates on four sides—three gates on the south, one each on east, west, and north.
translations.idiomatic: The inner enclosure stood fifteen zhang from the altar, eight chi one cun high, with Spirit Star gates on all four sides—three on the south and one each on the east, west, and north.

sentences.zh: 外垣去壝十五丈，門制同。

translations.literal: The outer wall was fifteen zhang from the enclosure, with gates of the same design.
translations.idiomatic: The outer wall stood fifteen zhang beyond the inner enclosure, with gates of the same design.

sentences.zh: 天下神祇壇東門外。

translations.literal: Outside the eastern gate of the Altar of All Spirits Under Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: It lay outside the eastern gate of the Altar of All Spirits Under Heaven.

sentences.zh: 神庫五楹，在外垣北，南向。

translations.literal: The spirit storehouse had five bays, north of the outer wall, facing south.
translations.idiomatic: The spirit storehouse had five bays, north of the outer wall, facing south.

sentences.zh: 廚房五楹祇，在外壇東北，西向。

translations.literal: The kitchen building had five bays, northeast of the outer altar, facing west.
translations.idiomatic: The kitchen building had five bays, northeast of the outer altar, facing west.

sentences.zh: 庫房五楹，南向。

translations.literal: The supply storehouse had five bays, facing south.
translations.idiomatic: The supply storehouse had five bays, facing south.

sentences.zh: 宰牲房三楹，天池一，又在外庫房之北。

translations.literal: The slaughtering building had three bays and one celestial pool, again north of the outer supply storehouse.
translations.idiomatic: The slaughtering building had three bays and a celestial pool, situated north of the outer supply storehouse.

sentences.zh: 執事齋舍，在壇外垣之東南。

translations.literal: The attendants' fasting quarters were southeast of the altar's outer wall.
translations.idiomatic: The attendants' fasting quarters stood southeast of the altar's outer wall.

sentences.zh: 坊二，在外門外橫甬道之東西，燎壇在內壝外東南丙地，高九尺，廣七尺，開上南出戶。

translations.literal: Two memorial arches stood east and west of the transverse passage outside the outer gate; the fire altar was in the southeast bing position outside the inner enclosure, nine chi high and seven chi wide, with an opening above and a door facing south.
translations.idiomatic: Two memorial arches stood east and west of the transverse passage outside the outer gate; the fire altar stood in the southeast bing position outside the inner enclosure, nine chi high and seven chi wide, with an opening above and a door facing south.

sentences.zh: 方丘壇二成。

translations.literal: The Square Mound altar had two tiers.
translations.idiomatic: The Square Mound altar had two tiers.

sentences.zh: 上成廣六丈，高六尺，四出陛，南一丈，東、西、北八尺，皆八級。

translations.literal: The upper tier was six zhang wide and six chi high, with steps on four sides; south one zhang, east, west, and north eight chi, all of eight steps.
translations.idiomatic: The upper tier measured six zhang across and six chi in height, with steps on all four sides; the southern stairway was one zhang wide, and those on the east, west, and north were eight chi, each with eight steps.

sentences.zh: 下成四面各廣二丈四尺，高六尺，四出陛，南丈二尺，東、西、北一丈，皆八級。

translations.literal: The lower tier on each of four sides was two zhang four chi wide and six chi high, with steps on four sides; south one zhang two chi, east, west, and north one zhang, all of eight steps.
translations.idiomatic: The lower tier measured two zhang four chi on each side and six chi in height, with steps on all four sides; the southern stairway was one zhang two chi wide, and those on the east, west, and north were one zhang, each with eight steps.

sentences.zh: 壝去壇十五丈，高六尺，外垣四面各六十四丈，餘制同。

translations.literal: The enclosure was fifteen zhang from the altar and six chi high; the outer wall on each of four sides was sixty-four zhang; the remaining regulations were the same.
translations.idiomatic: The inner enclosure stood fifteen zhang from the altar and six chi high; the outer wall measured sixty-four zhang on each side; the remaining specifications matched those of the Circular Mound.

sentences.zh: 南郊有浴室，瘞坎在內壝外壬地。

translations.literal: At the southern suburb there was a bathhouse; the burial pit was in the ren position outside the inner enclosure.
translations.idiomatic: At the southern suburb there was a bathhouse, and the burial pit for sacrificial offerings stood in the ren position outside the inner enclosure.

sentences.zh: 洪武四年，改築圜丘。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Hongwu, the Circular Mound was rebuilt.
translations.idiomatic: In Hongwu 4, the Circular Mound was rebuilt.

sentences.zh: 上成廣四丈五尺，高五尺二寸。

translations.literal: The upper tier was four zhang five chi wide and five chi two cun high.
translations.idiomatic: The upper tier measured four zhang five chi across and five chi two cun in height.

sentences.zh: 下成每面廣一丈六尺五寸，高四尺九寸。

translations.literal: Each face of the lower tier was one zhang six chi five cun wide and four chi nine cun high.
translations.idiomatic: Each side of the lower tier measured one zhang six chi five cun across and four chi nine cun in height.

sentences.zh: 二成通徑七丈八尺。

translations.literal: The total diameter of the two tiers was seven zhang eight chi.
translations.idiomatic: The combined diameter of the two tiers was seven zhang eight chi.

sentences.zh: 壇至內壝牆，四面各九丈八尺五寸。

translations.literal: From the altar to the inner enclosure wall, on each of four sides nine zhang eight chi five cun.
translations.idiomatic: The distance from the altar to the inner enclosure wall was nine zhang eight chi five cun on each side.

sentences.zh: 內壝牆至外壝牆，南十三丈九尺四寸，北十一丈，東、西各十一丈七尺。

translations.literal: From the inner enclosure wall to the outer enclosure wall: south thirteen zhang nine chi four cun, north eleven zhang, east and west each eleven zhang seven chi.
translations.idiomatic: From the inner to the outer enclosure wall: thirteen zhang nine chi four cun on the south, eleven zhang on the north, and eleven zhang seven chi on the east and west.

sentences.zh: 方丘，上成廣三丈九尺四寸，高三尺九寸。

translations.literal: The Square Mound: the upper tier was three zhang nine chi four cun wide and three chi nine cun high.
translations.idiomatic: For the Square Mound, the upper tier measured three zhang nine chi four cun across and three chi nine cun in height.

sentences.zh: 下成每面廣丈五尺五寸，高三尺八寸，通徑七丈四寸。

translations.literal: Each face of the lower tier was one zhang five chi five cun wide and three chi eight cun high; the total diameter was seven zhang four cun.
translations.idiomatic: Each side of the lower tier measured one zhang five chi five cun across and three chi eight cun in height, with a combined diameter of seven zhang four cun.

sentences.zh: 壇至內壝牆，四面皆八丈九尺五寸。

translations.literal: From the altar to the inner enclosure wall, on all four sides eight zhang nine chi five cun.
translations.idiomatic: The distance from the altar to the inner enclosure wall was eight zhang nine chi five cun on all four sides.

sentences.zh: 內壝牆至外壝牆，四面各八丈二尺。

translations.literal: From the inner enclosure wall to the outer enclosure wall, on each of four sides eight zhang two chi.
translations.idiomatic: From the inner to the outer enclosure wall, the distance was eight zhang two chi on each side.

sentences.zh: 十年，改定合祀之典。

translations.literal: In the tenth year, the canon of combined sacrifice was revised and fixed.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth year, the regulations for combined sacrifice were revised.

sentences.zh: 即圜丘舊制，而以屋覆之，名曰大祀殿，凡十二楹。

translations.literal: Taking the old Circular Mound design and roofing it with a building, it was named the Hall of Great Sacrifice, twelve bays in all.
translations.idiomatic: The old Circular Mound design was roofed over to form the Hall of Great Sacrifice, comprising twelve bays.

sentences.zh: 中石臺設上帝、皇地祇座。

translations.literal: At the central stone platform were set seats for the Supreme Lord and the August Sovereign Earth Spirit.
translations.idiomatic: At the central stone platform were placed the seats for the Supreme Lord of Heaven and the Sovereign Earth Spirit.

sentences.zh: 東、西廣三十二楹。

translations.literal: East and west were broadly thirty-two bays.
translations.idiomatic: The eastern and western wings each extended thirty-two bays.

sentences.zh: 正南大祀門六楹，接以步廊，與殿廡通。

translations.literal: Due south, the Great Sacrifice Gate had six bays, connected by a covered corridor to communicate with the hall wings.
translations.idiomatic: To the south, the Great Sacrifice Gate of six bays was connected by a covered corridor to the hall wings.

sentences.zh: 殿後天庫六楹。

translations.literal: Behind the hall, the Celestial Storehouse had six bays.
translations.idiomatic: Behind the hall stood the Celestial Storehouse of six bays.

sentences.zh: 瓦皆黃琉璃。

translations.literal: The tiles were all yellow glazed tile.
translations.idiomatic: All roof tiles were yellow glazed tile.

sentences.zh: 廚庫在殿東北，宰牲亭井在廚東北，皆以步廊通殿兩廡，後繚以圍牆。

translations.literal: The kitchen storehouse was northeast of the hall; the slaughtering pavilion and well were northeast of the kitchen—all connected by covered corridors to the two hall wings, and afterward enclosed by a surrounding wall.
translations.idiomatic: The kitchen and storehouse stood northeast of the hall, with the slaughtering pavilion and well northeast of the kitchen; covered corridors connected them to both hall wings, and the complex was enclosed by a surrounding wall.

sentences.zh: 南爲石門三洞以達大祀門，謂之內壇。

translations.literal: To the south were three stone gate openings leading to the Great Sacrifice Gate, called the inner altar.
translations.idiomatic: To the south, three stone gate openings led to the Great Sacrifice Gate, forming the inner altar.

sentences.zh: 外周垣九里三十步，石門三洞南爲甬道三，中神道，左御道，右王道。

translations.literal: The outer surrounding wall was nine li thirty bu; south of the three stone gate openings were three passages—the central spirit way, the left imperial way, and the right kingly way.
translations.idiomatic: The outer wall measured nine li thirty bu in circumference; south of the three stone gate openings ran three passages—the central spirit way, the imperial way on the left, and the kingly way on the right.

sentences.zh: 道兩旁稍低，爲從官之地。

translations.literal: On both sides of the ways, slightly lower, was the ground for attending officials.
translations.idiomatic: Slightly lower ground on either side of the passages was reserved for attending officials.

sentences.zh: 齋宮在外垣內西南，東向。

translations.literal: The fasting palace was southwest within the outer wall, facing east.
translations.idiomatic: The fasting palace stood in the southwest within the outer wall, facing east.

sentences.zh: 其後殿瓦易青琉璃。

translations.literal: Later the hall tiles were changed to blue glazed tile.
translations.idiomatic: Later the hall's roof tiles were changed to blue glazed tile.

sentences.zh: 二十一年增修壇壝，壇後樹松柏，外壝東南鑿池二十區。

translations.literal: In the twenty-first year the altar and enclosure were enlarged and repaired; pine and cypress were planted behind the altar, and twenty pools were excavated in the southeast of the outer enclosure.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-first year the altar and enclosures were enlarged and repaired; pine and cypress were planted behind the altar, and twenty pools were excavated in the southeast of the outer enclosure.

sentences.zh: 冬月伐冰藏凌陰，以供夏秋祭祀之用。

translations.literal: In the winter months ice was cut and stored in the ice cellar to supply the needs of spring-summer and autumn sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: In winter ice was harvested and stored in the ice cellar for use in the spring, summer, and autumn sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 成祖遷都北京，如其制。

translations.literal: The Chengzu Emperor moved the capital to Beijing and followed the same design.
translations.idiomatic: When the Yongle Emperor transferred the capital to Beijing, he replicated the same design.

sentences.zh: 嘉靖九年，復改分祀。

translations.literal: In the ninth year of Jiajing, separate sacrifices were again restored.
translations.idiomatic: In Jiajing 9, the practice of separate sacrifices was restored.

sentences.zh: 建圜丘壇於正陽門外五里許，大祀殿之南，方澤壇於安定門外之東。

translations.literal: The Circular Mound altar was built about five li outside the Gate of Correct Yang, south of the Hall of Great Sacrifice; the Square Mound altar was built to the east, outside the Gate of Stability.
translations.idiomatic: The Circular Mound altar was erected roughly five li outside the Gate of Correct Yang, south of the Hall of Great Sacrifice; the Square Mound altar was built to the east, outside the Gate of Stability.

sentences.zh: 圜丘二成，壇面及欄俱青琉璃，邊角用白玉石，高廣尺寸皆遵祖制，而神路轉遠。

translations.literal: The Circular Mound had two tiers; the altar surface and railings were all blue glazed tile, corners using white jade stone; height and breadth all followed ancestral regulations, but the spirit way became longer.
translations.idiomatic: The Circular Mound comprised two tiers, with blue glazed tile on the altar surface and railings and white jade at the corners; its dimensions followed ancestral precedent, though the spirit way was lengthened.

sentences.zh: 內門四。

translations.literal: Inner gates: four.
translations.idiomatic: Inner gates: four.

sentences.zh: 南門外燎爐毛血池，西南望燎臺。

translations.literal: Outside the south gate were the burning furnace and fur-and-blood pool; southwest was the Watch-Burning Platform.
translations.idiomatic: Outside the south gate stood the burning furnace and fur-and-blood pool; to the southwest was the Watch-Burning Platform.

sentences.zh: 外門亦四。

translations.literal: Outer gates also four.
translations.idiomatic: There were likewise four outer gates.

sentences.zh: 南門外左具服臺，東門外神庫、神廚、祭器庫、宰牲亭，北門外正北泰神殿。

translations.literal: Outside the south gate to the left was the Robing Platform; outside the east gate the Spirit Storehouse, Spirit Kitchen, Ritual Vessel Storehouse, and Slaughtering Pavilion; directly north outside the north gate was the Hall of Supreme Deity.
translations.idiomatic: To the left outside the south gate stood the Robing Platform; outside the east gate were the Spirit Storehouse, Spirit Kitchen, Ritual Vessel Storehouse, and Slaughtering Pavilion; directly north of the north gate stood the Hall of Supreme Deity.

sentences.zh: 正殿以藏上帝、太祖之主，配殿以藏從祀諸神之王。

translations.literal: The main hall stored the tablets of the Supreme Lord and the Grand Progenitor; the side halls stored the tablets of the attendant deities in the collateral sacrifice.
translations.idiomatic: The main hall housed the spirit tablets of the Supreme Lord and Grand Progenitor Taizu; the side halls held those of the attendant deities offered in collateral sacrifice.

sentences.zh: 外建四天門：東曰泰元，南曰昭亭，西曰廣利。

translations.literal: Outside four Heavenly Gates were built: east called Taiyuan, south called Zhaoting, west called Guangli.
translations.idiomatic: Four Heavenly Gates were built on the outside: Taiyuan to the east, Zhaoting to the south, and Guangli to the west.

sentences.zh: 又西鑾駕庫，又西犧牲所，其北神樂觀。

translations.literal: Further west the Imperial Carriage Storehouse; further west the Sacrificial Livestock Office; north of it the Spirit Music Observatory.
translations.idiomatic: Farther west stood the Imperial Carriage Storehouse, and beyond that the Sacrificial Livestock Office; to its north stood the Spirit Music Observatory.

sentences.zh: 北曰成貞。

translations.literal: North called Chengzhen.
translations.idiomatic: To the north was Chengzhen Gate.

sentences.zh: 北門外西北爲齋宮，迤西爲壇門，壇北，舊天地壇，即大祀殿也。

translations.literal: Northwest outside the north gate was the Fasting Palace; winding west was the altar gate; north of the altar, the old Altar of Heaven and Earth, namely the Hall of Great Sacrifice.
translations.idiomatic: Northwest of the north gate stood the Fasting Palace; westward along the perimeter was the altar gate; north of the altar stood the old Altar of Heaven and Earth—that is, the Hall of Great Sacrifice.

sentences.zh: 十七年撤之，又改泰神殿曰皇穹宇。

translations.literal: In the seventeenth year it was removed; the Hall of Supreme Deity was also renamed the Imperial Vault of Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventeenth year it was dismantled, and the Hall of Supreme Deity was renamed the Imperial Vault of Heaven.

sentences.zh: 二十四年，又即故大祀殿之址建大享殿。

translations.literal: In the twenty-fourth year, again on the site of the former Hall of Great Sacrifice the Hall of Great Offering was built.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-fourth year, the Hall of Great Offering was erected on the former site of the Hall of Great Sacrifice.

sentences.zh: 方澤亦二成，壇面黃琉璃，陛增爲九級，用白石圍以方坎。

translations.literal: The Square Mound likewise had two tiers; the altar surface yellow glazed tile; steps increased to nine grades; white stone encircled a square depression.
translations.idiomatic: The Square Mound also had two tiers, with a yellow glazed altar surface; the steps were raised to nine grades, and white stone enclosed a square sunken pool.

sentences.zh: 內，北門外西瘞位，東燈臺，南門外皇祇室。

translations.literal: Within: west outside the north gate the burial place; east the lamp platform; outside the south gate the Chamber of the August Earth Spirit.
translations.idiomatic: Within the inner enclosure: west of the north gate was the burial place for sacrificial remains; to the east a lamp platform; outside the south gate stood the Chamber of the Sovereign Earth Spirit.

sentences.zh: 外，西門外迤西神庫、神廚、宰牲亭、祭器庫，北門外西北齋宮。

translations.literal: Without: west of the west gate further west Spirit Storehouse, Spirit Kitchen, Slaughtering Pavilion, Ritual Vessel Storehouse; northwest outside the north gate the Fasting Palace.
translations.idiomatic: Outside the inner enclosure: west of the west gate were, in succession, the Spirit Storehouse, Spirit Kitchen, Slaughtering Pavilion, and Ritual Vessel Storehouse; northwest of the north gate stood the Fasting Palace.

sentences.zh: 又外建四天門，西門外北爲鑾駕庫、遣官房、內陪祀官房。

translations.literal: Further outside four Heavenly Gates were built; north outside the west gate the Imperial Carriage Storehouse, dispatch-official quarters, and inner collateral-sacrifice official quarters.
translations.idiomatic: Four more Heavenly Gates were built still farther out; north of the west gate were the Imperial Carriage Storehouse, quarters for dispatched officials, and rooms for inner collateral-sacrifice attendants.

sentences.zh: 又外爲壇門，門外爲泰折街牌坊，護壇地千四百餘畝。

translations.literal: Still further outside were altar gates; outside the gates the Taizhe Street memorial archway; protected altar grounds over fourteen hundred mu.
translations.idiomatic: Beyond these stood the altar gates, and outside them the Taizhe Street memorial archway, with more than fourteen hundred mu of land set aside to protect the altar precinct.

sentences.zh: 太社稷壇，在宮城西南，東西峙，明初建。

translations.literal: The Great Altars of Soil and Grain were southwest of the palace city, standing east and west facing each other; built at the beginning of the Ming.
translations.idiomatic: The Great Altars of Soil and Grain stood southwest of the palace city, facing each other east and west; they were built early in the dynasty.

sentences.zh: 廣五丈，高五尺，四出陛，皆五級。

translations.literal: Breadth five zhang, height five chi, steps on four sides, all five grades.
translations.idiomatic: Each measured five zhang across and five chi high, with steps on all four sides rising in five grades.

sentences.zh: 壇土五色隨其方，黃土覆之。

translations.literal: Altar soil five colors according to direction; yellow soil covered it.
translations.idiomatic: The altar soil was colored according to the five directions, with yellow earth spread on top.

sentences.zh: 壇相去五丈，壇南皆樹鬆。

translations.literal: The altars were five zhang apart; south of the altars all planted pine.
translations.idiomatic: The two altars stood five zhang apart, and pines were planted south of each.

sentences.zh: 二壇同一壝，方廣三十丈，高五尺，甃磚，四門飾色隨其方。

translations.literal: The two altars shared one enclosure; square breadth thirty zhang, height five chi, paved with brick; four gates decorated in colors according to direction.
translations.idiomatic: Both altars shared a single enclosure thirty zhang square and five chi high, paved with brick; the four gates were painted in the colors of their respective directions.

sentences.zh: 周坦四門，南靈星門三，北戟門五，東西戟門三。

translations.literal: Around the level ground four gates: south three Spirit Star gates, north five halberd gates, east and west three halberd gates each.
translations.idiomatic: A level plaza was ringed by four gates: three Spirit Star gates on the south, five halberd gates on the north, and three halberd gates each on the east and west.

sentences.zh: 戟門各列戟二十四。

translations.literal: Each halberd gate displayed twenty-four halberds.
translations.idiomatic: Each halberd gate displayed twenty-four halberds in rank.

sentences.zh: 洪武十年，改壇午門右，社稷共一罈，爲二成。

translations.literal: In Hongwu 10, the altars were moved to the right of the Meridian Gate; soil and grain shared one mound, made two tiers.
translations.idiomatic: In Hongwu 10 the altars were relocated to the right of the Meridian Gate, with the soil and grain altars combined on a single two-tiered mound.

sentences.zh: 上成廣五丈，下成廣五丈三尺，崇五尺。

translations.literal: Upper tier breadth five zhang; lower tier breadth five zhang three chi; elevation five chi.
translations.idiomatic: The upper tier measured five zhang across, the lower five zhang three chi, with a total elevation of five chi.

sentences.zh: 外壝崇五尺，四面各十九丈有奇。

translations.literal: Outer enclosure elevation five chi; each of the four sides nineteen-odd zhang.
translations.idiomatic: The outer enclosure rose five chi, with each side measuring a little over nineteen zhang.

sentences.zh: 外垣東西六十六丈有奇，南北八十六丈有奇。

translations.literal: Outer wall east-west sixty-six-odd zhang, north-south eighty-six-odd zhang.
translations.idiomatic: The outer wall measured a little over sixty-six zhang east to west and eighty-six zhang north to south.

sentences.zh: 垣北三門，門外爲祭殿，其北爲拜殿。

translations.literal: North of the wall three gates; outside the gates the offering hall, north of it the bowing hall.
translations.idiomatic: Three gates opened on the north side of the wall; beyond them stood the offering hall, and north of that the bowing hall.

sentences.zh: 外復爲三門，垣東、西、南門各一。

translations.literal: Outside again three gates; east, west, and south of the wall one each.
translations.idiomatic: Three more gates stood outside, one each on the east, west, and south sides of the wall.

sentences.zh: 永樂中，建壇北京，如其制。

translations.literal: In the Yongle reign, altars were built in Beijing according to the design.
translations.idiomatic: During the Yongle reign, altars were erected in Beijing to the same specifications.

sentences.zh: 帝社稷壇在西苑，壇址高六寸，方廣二丈五尺，甃細磚，實以淨土。

translations.literal: The emperor's altars of soil and grain were in the Western Park; the altar base six cun high, square breadth two zhang five chi, paved with fine brick, packed with pure soil.
translations.idiomatic: The imperial altars of soil and grain stood in the Western Park; the altar base was six cun high and two zhang five chi square, paved with fine brick and packed with pure earth.

sentences.zh: 壇北樹二坊，曰社街。

translations.literal: North of the altar two memorial arches were erected, called She Street.
translations.idiomatic: North of the altar stood two memorial arches marking She Street.

sentences.zh: 王國社稷壇，高廣殺太社稷十之三。

translations.literal: Princely kingdom altars of soil and grain: height and breadth reduced by three-tenths from the Great Altars.
translations.idiomatic: In princely domains the altars of soil and grain were reduced in height and breadth by three-tenths from those of the capital.

sentences.zh: 府、州、縣社稷壇，廣殺十之五，高殺十之四，陛三級。

translations.literal: Prefecture, department, and county altars: breadth reduced five-tenths, height four-tenths, steps three grades.
translations.idiomatic: At prefecture, department, and county levels, the altars were five-tenths narrower and four-tenths lower, with steps of three grades.

sentences.zh: 後皆定同壇合祭，如京師。

translations.literal: Later all were fixed as combined sacrifice on a single altar, as in the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Later all jurisdictions were required to offer combined sacrifice at a single altar, as in the capital.

sentences.zh: 朝日、夕月壇，洪武三年建。

translations.literal: Morning Sun and Evening Moon altars, built in Hongwu 3.
translations.idiomatic: The Morning Sun and Evening Moon altars were built in Hongwu 3.

sentences.zh: 朝日壇高八尺，夕月壇高六尺，俱方廣四丈。

translations.literal: Morning Sun altar eight chi high, Evening Moon altar six chi high; both square four zhang breadth.
translations.idiomatic: The Morning Sun altar stood eight chi high and the Evening Moon altar six chi, each four zhang square.

sentences.zh: 兩壝，壝各二十五步。

translations.literal: Two enclosures; each enclosure twenty-five paces.
translations.idiomatic: Each altar had two enclosures, each measuring twenty-five paces.

sentences.zh: 二十一年罷。

translations.literal: Abolished in the twenty-first year.
translations.idiomatic: They were abolished in the twenty-first year.

sentences.zh: 嘉靖九年復建，壇各一成。

translations.literal: Rebuilt in Jiajing 9; each altar one tier.
translations.idiomatic: They were rebuilt in Jiajing 9, each altar with a single tier.

sentences.zh: 朝日壇紅琉璃，夕月壇用白。

translations.literal: Morning Sun altar red glazed tile; Evening Moon altar used white.
translations.idiomatic: The Morning Sun altar used red glazed tile; the Evening Moon altar used white.

sentences.zh: 朝日壇陛九級，夕月壇六級，俱白石。

translations.literal: Morning Sun altar steps nine grades, Evening Moon six grades; all white stone.
translations.idiomatic: The Morning Sun altar had nine steps and the Evening Moon six, all of white stone.

sentences.zh: 各建天門二。

translations.literal: Each built two Heavenly Gates.
translations.idiomatic: Each altar was provided with two Heavenly Gates.

sentences.zh: 先農壇，高五尺，廣五丈，四出陛。

translations.literal: Agriculture Ancestor Altar, five chi high, five zhang broad, steps on four sides.
translations.idiomatic: The Agriculture Ancestor Altar stood five chi high and five zhang across, with steps on all four sides.

sentences.zh: 御耕耤位，高三尺，廣二丈五尺，四出陛。

translations.literal: Imperial plowing position, three chi high, two zhang five chi broad, steps on four sides.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor's plowing platform was three chi high and two zhang five chi across, with steps on all four sides.

sentences.zh: 山川壇，洪武九年建。

translations.literal: Mountains and Rivers Altar, built Hongwu 9.
translations.idiomatic: The Mountains and Rivers Altar was built in Hongwu 9.

sentences.zh: 正殿、拜殿各八楹，東西廡二十四楹。

translations.literal: Main hall and bowing hall each eight bays; east-west corridors twenty-four bays.
translations.idiomatic: The main hall and bowing hall each had eight bays, with east and west corridors of twenty-four bays.

sentences.zh: 西南先農壇，東南具服殿，殿南耤田壇，東旗纛廟，後爲神倉。

translations.literal: Southwest the Agriculture Ancestor Altar; southeast the Robing Hall; south of the hall the plowing-field altar; east the Banner and Pennant Shrine; behind was the Spirit Granary.
translations.idiomatic: Southwest stood the Agriculture Ancestor Altar; southeast, the Robing Hall; south of the hall, the plowing-field altar; to the east, the Banner and Pennant Shrine; and behind them, the Spirit Granary.

sentences.zh: 周垣七百餘丈，垣內地歲種穀蔬，供祀事。

translations.literal: Surrounding wall over seven hundred zhang; land within the wall each year planted grain and vegetables to supply sacrificial affairs.
translations.idiomatic: The surrounding wall exceeded seven hundred zhang in circumference; crops and vegetables were planted within each year to supply the sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 嘉靖十年，改名天神地祇壇，分列左右。

translations.literal: Jiajing 10, renamed Heavenly Spirits and Earthly Sovereigns Altar, arranged left and right separately.
translations.idiomatic: In Jiajing 10 it was renamed the Altar of Heavenly Spirits and Earthly Sovereigns and divided into separate sections on the left and right.

sentences.zh: 太歲壇與嶽瀆同。

translations.literal: Grand Year Star Altar the same as peaks and rivers.
translations.idiomatic: The Grand Year Star altar followed the same design as those for sacred peaks and rivers.

sentences.zh: 嶽鎮海瀆山川城隍壇，據高阜，南向，高二尺五寸，方廣十倍，四出陛，南向五級，東西北三級。

translations.literal: Altars for peaks, garrisons, seas, rivers, mountains and rivers, and city gods: occupying high mounds, facing south, two chi five cun high, square breadth tenfold, steps on four sides—south five grades, east north west three grades.
translations.idiomatic: Altars for sacred peaks, garrisons, seas, rivers, mountains, and city gods were placed on high ground facing south; they measured two chi five cun high and ten times that in breadth, with steps on all four sides—five on the south and three on the east, north, and west.

sentences.zh: 王國山川壇，高四尺，四出陛，方三丈五尺。

translations.literal: Princely kingdom mountains-and-rivers altar, four chi high, steps four sides, square three zhang five chi.
translations.idiomatic: In princely domains the mountains-and-rivers altar stood four chi high and three zhang five chi square, with steps on all four sides.

sentences.zh: 天下山川所在壇，高三尺，四出陛，三級，方二丈五尺。

translations.literal: Altars wherever mountains and rivers exist under heaven, three chi high, steps four sides, three grades, square two zhang five chi.
translations.idiomatic: Altars erected wherever significant mountains and rivers existed under heaven stood three chi high and two zhang five chi square, with steps on all four sides in three grades.

sentences.zh: ○神位祭器玉帛牲牢祝冊之數

translations.literal: ○ Numbers of spirit seats, ritual vessels, silks, sacrificial animals, and prayer documents
translations.idiomatic: ○ Numbers of Spirit Seats, Ritual Vessels, Silks, Sacrificial Animals, and Prayer Scrolls

sentences.zh: 神位圜丘。

translations.literal: Spirit seats: Circular Mound.
translations.idiomatic: Spirit Seats: The Circular Mound.

sentences.zh: 洪武元年冬至，正壇第一成，昊天上帝南向。

translations.literal: Hongwu 1 winter solstice, main altar first tier, Supreme Lord of Heaven facing south.
translations.idiomatic: At the winter solstice of Hongwu 1, on the first tier of the main altar, the Supreme Lord of Heaven faced south.

sentences.zh: 第二成，東大明，星辰次之，西夜明，太歲次之。

translations.literal: Second tier: east Great Brightness, stars and constellations next; west Night Brightness, Grand Year Star next.
translations.idiomatic: On the second tier: to the east stood Great Brightness, with the stars and constellations beside it; to the west stood Night Brightness, with the Grand Year Star beside it.

sentences.zh: 二年，奉仁祖配，位第一成，西向。

translations.literal: Second year, Benevolent Ancestor offered as collateral, seat first tier, facing west.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year the Benevolent Ancestor was installed as collateral at the first tier, facing west.

sentences.zh: 三年，壇下壝內，增祭風雲雷雨。

translations.literal: Third year, within the enclosure below the altar, added sacrifice to wind, clouds, thunder, and rain.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year, within the enclosure below the altar, wind, clouds, thunder, and rain were added to the sacrifice.

sentences.zh: 七年更定，內壝之內，東西各三壇。

translations.literal: Seventh year revised and fixed: within the inner enclosure, east and west each three altars.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year the arrangement was revised: within the inner enclosure were three altars each on the east and west.

sentences.zh: 星辰二壇，分設於東西。

translations.literal: Stars and constellations two altars, separately set east and west.
translations.idiomatic: The stars and constellations occupied two altars, one on the east and one on the west.

sentences.zh: 其次，東則太歲、五嶽，西則風雲雨、五鎮。

translations.literal: Next to them: east then Grand Year Star, Five Peaks; west then wind, clouds, rain, Five Garrisons.
translations.idiomatic: Beside them: on the east were the Grand Year Star and the Five Peaks; on the west, wind, clouds, and rain, and the Five Garrisons.

sentences.zh: 內壝之外，東西各二壇。

translations.literal: Outside the inner enclosure, east and west each two altars.
translations.idiomatic: Outside the inner enclosure were two altars each on the east and west.

sentences.zh: 東四海，西四瀆。

translations.literal: East Four Seas, west Four Rivers.
translations.idiomatic: On the east were the Four Seas; on the west, the Four Rivers.

sentences.zh: 次天下神祇壇，東西分設。

translations.literal: Next the All-under-Heaven Spirits and Earthly Powers altar, set separately east and west.
translations.idiomatic: Next came the altars for spirits and earthly powers throughout the realm, one on the east and one on the west.

sentences.zh: 方丘。

translations.literal: Square Mound.
translations.idiomatic: Square Mound.

sentences.zh: 洪武二年夏至，正壇第一成，皇地祇，南向。

translations.literal: Hongwu 2 summer solstice, main altar first tier, Sovereign Earth Spirit, facing south.
translations.idiomatic: At the summer solstice of Hongwu 2, on the first tier of the main altar, the Sovereign Earth Spirit faced south.

sentences.zh: 第二成，東五嶽，次四海，西五鎮，次四瀆。

translations.literal: Second tier: east Five Peaks, next Four Seas; west Five Garrisons, next Four Rivers.
translations.idiomatic: On the second tier: to the east were the Five Peaks, with the Four Seas beside them; to the west were the Five Garrisons, with the Four Rivers beside them.

sentences.zh: 三年，奉仁祖配，位第一成，西向。

translations.literal: Third year, Benevolent Ancestor collateral, seat first tier, facing west.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year the Benevolent Ancestor was installed as collateral at the first tier, facing west.

sentences.zh: 壇下壝內，增祭天下山川。

translations.literal: Within the enclosure below the altar, added sacrifice to all mountains and rivers under heaven.
translations.idiomatic: Within the enclosure below the altar, all mountains and rivers under heaven were added to the sacrifice.

sentences.zh: 七年更定，內壝之內，東西各二壇。

translations.literal: Seventh year revised: within inner enclosure, east and west each two altars.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year the arrangement was revised: within the inner enclosure were two altars each on the east and west.

sentences.zh: 東四海，西四瀆。

translations.literal: East Four Seas, west Four Rivers.
translations.idiomatic: On the east were the Four Seas; on the west, the Four Rivers.

sentences.zh: 次二壇，天下山川。

translations.literal: Next two altars, all mountains and rivers.
translations.idiomatic: Next came two altars for all mountains and rivers.

sentences.zh: 內壝之外，東西各設天下神祇壇一。

translations.literal: Outside inner enclosure, east and west each one All-under-Heaven Spirits and Earthly Powers altar set.
translations.idiomatic: Outside the inner enclosure, one altar for spirits and earthly powers throughout the realm was placed on each side, east and west.

sentences.zh: 十二年正月，合祀大祀殿。

translations.literal: Twelfth year first month, combined sacrifice at Hall of Great Sacrifice.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the twelfth year, combined sacrifice was performed at the Hall of Great Sacrifice.

sentences.zh: 正殿三壇，上帝、皇地祇並南向。

translations.literal: Main hall three altars; Supreme Lord and Sovereign Earth Spirit both facing south.
translations.idiomatic: The main hall held three altars: the Supreme Lord and Sovereign Earth Spirit both faced south.

sentences.zh: 仁祖配位在東，西向。

translations.literal: Benevolent Ancestor collateral seat east, facing west.
translations.idiomatic: The Benevolent Ancestor's collateral seat stood to the east, facing west.

sentences.zh: 從祀十四壇。

translations.literal: Collateral sacrifice fourteen altars.
translations.idiomatic: Fourteen altars served for collateral sacrifice.

sentences.zh: 丹陛東一罈曰大明，西一罈曰夜明。

translations.literal: On the red steps east one mound called Great Brightness, west one mound called Night Brightness.
translations.idiomatic: On the red steps, one mound to the east was named Great Brightness and one to the west Night Brightness.

sentences.zh: 兩廡壇各六：星辰二壇；

translations.literal: Both corridor altars six each: stars and constellations two altars;
translations.idiomatic: The two corridor wings held six altars each: two for the stars and constellations;

sentences.zh: 次東，太歲、五嶽、四海，次西，風雲雷雨、五鎮、四瀆二壇；

translations.literal: Next east: Grand Year Star, Five Peaks, Four Seas; next west: wind clouds thunder rain, Five Garrisons, Four Rivers two altars;
translations.idiomatic: Next on the east, the Grand Year Star, Five Peaks, and Four Seas; next on the west, wind, clouds, thunder, and rain, the Five Garrisons, and two altars for the Four Rivers;

sentences.zh: 又次天下山川神祇二壇。

translations.literal: Again next all-under-heaven mountains rivers spirits earthly powers two altars.
translations.idiomatic: And beyond them, two altars for mountains, rivers, and spirits throughout the realm.

sentences.zh: 俱東西向。

translations.literal: All facing east and west.
translations.idiomatic: All faced east or west.

sentences.zh: 二十一年，增修丹墀內石臺四，大明、夜明各一，星辰二。

translations.literal: Twenty-first year, enlarged and repaired within red courtyard four stone platforms: Great Brightness, Night Brightness one each, stars and constellations two.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-first year four stone platforms were added within the red courtyard: one each for Great Brightness and Night Brightness, and two for the stars and constellations.

sentences.zh: 內壝外石臺二十：東十壇，北嶽、北鎮、東嶽、東鎮、東海、太歲、帝王、山川、神祇、四瀆；

translations.literal: Outside inner enclosure twenty stone platforms: east ten altars—North Peak, North Garrison, East Peak, East Garrison, East Sea, Grand Year Star, emperors, mountains rivers, spirits earthly powers, Four Rivers;
translations.idiomatic: Outside the inner enclosure stood twenty stone platforms: ten on the east—for the Northern Peak, Northern Garrison, Eastern Peak, Eastern Garrison, Eastern Sea, Grand Year Star, successive emperors, mountains and rivers, spirits and earthly powers, and the Four Rivers;

sentences.zh: 西十壇，北海、西嶽、西鎮、西海、中嶽、中鎮、風雲雷雨、南嶽、南鎮、南海。

translations.literal: West ten altars: North Sea, West Peak, West Garrison, West Sea, Central Peak, Central Garrison, wind clouds thunder rain, South Peak, South Garrison, South Sea.
translations.idiomatic: Ten on the west—for the Northern Sea, Western Peak, Western Garrison, Western Sea, Central Peak, Central Garrison, wind, clouds, thunder, and rain, Southern Peak, Southern Garrison, and Southern Sea.

sentences.zh: 俱東西向。

translations.literal: All facing east and west.
translations.idiomatic: All faced east or west.

sentences.zh: 臺高三尺有奇，周以石欄，陟降爲磴道。

translations.literal: Platforms three-odd chi high, encircled with stone rails; ascent and descent by stepped ramps.
translations.idiomatic: Each platform stood a little over three chi high, ringed with stone balustrades, with stepped ramps for ascent and descent.

sentences.zh: 臺上琢石鑿龕，以置神位。

translations.literal: On the platforms carved stone niches were chiseled to place spirit seats.
translations.idiomatic: Niches were carved into the stone platforms to hold the spirit seats.

sentences.zh: 建文時，撤仁祖，改奉太祖配，位第一成。

translations.literal: During the Jianwen reign, Benevolent Ancestor was removed; changed to offer Grand Progenitor as collateral, seat first tier.
translations.idiomatic: During the Jianwen reign the Benevolent Ancestor was removed, and Grand Progenitor Taizu was installed as collateral at the first tier.

sentences.zh: 西向。

translations.literal: Facing west.
translations.idiomatic: He faced west.

sentences.zh: 洪熙元年，增文皇帝於太祖下。

translations.literal: Hongxi 1, added the Literary Emperor below the Grand Progenitor.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Hongxi, the Literary Emperor was added below Grand Progenitor Taizu.

sentences.zh: 嘉靖九年，復分祀之典。

translations.literal: Jiajing 9, again restored the canon of separate sacrifice.
translations.idiomatic: In Jiajing 9 the regulations for separate sacrifice were restored.

sentences.zh: 圜丘則東大明，西夜明。

translations.literal: Circular Mound then east Great Brightness, west Night Brightness.
translations.idiomatic: At the Circular Mound, Great Brightness stood to the east and Night Brightness to the west.

sentences.zh: 次東，二十八宿、五星、周天星辰。

translations.literal: Next east: twenty-eight lunar lodges, five planets, all heaven stars and constellations.
translations.idiomatic: Next on the east stood the Twenty-eight Lunar Mansions, the Five Planets, and all the stars of the heavens.

sentences.zh: 次西，風雲雷雨。

translations.literal: Next west: wind, clouds, thunder, and rain.
translations.idiomatic: Next on the west stood wind, clouds, thunder, and rain.

sentences.zh: 共四壇。

translations.literal: Altogether four altars.
translations.idiomatic: There were four altars in all.

sentences.zh: 方丘則東五嶽，基運、翊聖、神烈三山，西五鎮，天壽、純德二山。

translations.literal: Square Mound then east Five Peaks, the three mountains Ji-yun, Yi-sheng, and Shen-lie; west Five Garrisons, the two mountains Tian-shou and Chun-de.
translations.idiomatic: At the Square Mound, to the east stood the Five Peaks and the three mountains of Ji-yun, Yi-sheng, and Shen-lie; to the west, the Five Garrisons and the two mountains of Tian-shou and Chun-de.

sentences.zh: 次東四海，次西四瀆。

translations.literal: Next east Four Seas, next west Four Rivers.
translations.idiomatic: Next on the east were the Four Seas; next on the west, the Four Rivers.

sentences.zh: 南北郊皆獨奉太祖配。

translations.literal: Northern and southern suburban sacrifices all exclusively offered Grand Progenitor as collateral.
translations.idiomatic: At both the northern and southern suburban sacrifices, Grand Progenitor Taizu alone was offered as collateral.

sentences.zh: 太社稷配位別見。

translations.literal: Great Altars of Soil and Grain collateral seats are separately recorded.
translations.idiomatic: The collateral seats at the Great Altars of Soil and Grain are recorded separately.

sentences.zh: 先農正位南向，后稷配位西向。

translations.literal: Agriculture Ancestor main seat facing south; Hou Ji collateral seat facing west.
translations.idiomatic: The Agriculture Ancestor's main seat faced south, and Hou Ji's collateral seat faced west.

sentences.zh: 凡神位，天地、祖宗曰：「神版」，餘曰：「神牌」。

translations.literal: For all spirit seats, Heaven and Earth and ancestors were called "spirit boards"; the rest were called "spirit tablets."
translations.idiomatic: For all spirit seats, Heaven, Earth, and the ancestors were termed "spirit boards," while all others were termed "spirit tablets."

sentences.zh: 圜丘神版長二尺五寸，廣五寸，厚一寸，趺高五寸，以慄木爲之，正位題曰昊天上帝，配位題曰某祖某皇帝，並黃質金字。

translations.literal: Circular Mound spirit board two chi five cun long, five cun wide, one cun thick, base five cun high, made of chestnut wood; main seat inscribed "August Supreme Lord of Heaven," collateral inscribed "Such-and-such Ancestor Such-and-such Emperor," all yellow with gold characters.
translations.idiomatic: The Circular Mound spirit board measured two chi five cun long, five cun wide, and one cun thick, with a base five cun high, and was made of chestnut wood. The main seat was inscribed "Supreme Lord of Heaven," and the collateral seat "Such-and-such Ancestor, Such-and-such Emperor"; both were yellow with gold lettering.

sentences.zh: 從祀風雲雷雨位版，赤質金字。

translations.literal: Collateral wind, clouds, thunder, and rain seat boards, red with gold characters.
translations.idiomatic: The seat boards for wind, clouds, thunder, and rain in collateral sacrifice were red with gold lettering.

sentences.zh: 神席，上帝用龍椅龍案，上施錦褥，配位同。

translations.literal: Spirit seats: the Supreme Lord used dragon throne and dragon table, with brocade cushion on top; collateral the same.
translations.idiomatic: For spirit seats, the Supreme Lord used a dragon throne and dragon table topped with a brocade cushion; the collateral seat was furnished the same way.

sentences.zh: 從祀，位置於案，不設席。

translations.literal: Collateral sacrifice: seats placed on tables, no cushions set.
translations.idiomatic: For collateral sacrifice, the seats were placed on tables and no cushions were provided.

sentences.zh: 方丘正位曰皇地祇，配位及從祀，制並同圜丘。

translations.literal: Square Mound main seat titled Sovereign Earth Spirit; collateral and collateral sacrifice, specifications all same as Circular Mound.
translations.idiomatic: The Square Mound main seat was titled Sovereign Earth Spirit; the collateral seat and all collateral sacrifices followed the same specifications as at the Circular Mound.

sentences.zh: 奉先殿帝后神主高尺二寸，廣四寸，趺高二寸，用木，飾以金，鏤以青字。

translations.literal: Hall of Ancestors emperor and empress spirit tablets one chi two cun high, four cun wide, base two cun high, of wood, decorated with gold, engraved with blue characters.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor's and empress's spirit tablets in the Hall of Ancestors stood one chi two cun high and four cun wide, with a base two cun high. They were of wood, gilded, and engraved with blue characters.

sentences.zh: 龕高二尺，廣二尺，趺高四寸，硃漆鏤金龍鳳花版，開二窗，施紅紗，側用金銅環，內織金文綺爲藉。

translations.literal: Shrine two chi high, two chi wide, base four cun high, red lacquer with gold-engraved dragon, phoenix, and floral panels; two windows opened, red gauze applied, gold and bronze rings on the sides, gold-patterned brocade woven inside as lining.
translations.idiomatic: The shrine stood two chi high and two chi wide, with a base four cun high, finished in red lacquer with gold-engraved panels of dragons, phoenixes, and flowers. It had two windows fitted with red gauze, gold and bronze rings on the sides, and gold-patterned brocade woven inside as a lining.

sentences.zh: 社稷，社玉用石，高五尺，廣五尺，上微銳。

translations.literal: Soil and grain altars: the altar of soil spirit object used stone, five chi high, five chi wide, slightly pointed at the top.
translations.idiomatic: At the altars of soil and grain, the altar of soil used a stone spirit object five chi high and five chi wide, slightly pointed at the top.

sentences.zh: 立於壇上，半在土中，近南北向；

translations.literal: Stood on the altar, half buried in the earth, nearly facing north-south;
translations.idiomatic: It stood on the altar, half buried in the earth, and nearly faced north and south;

sentences.zh: 稷不用主。

translations.literal: The grain altar used no spirit object.
translations.idiomatic: The altar of grain used no spirit object.

sentences.zh: 洪武十年，皆設木主，丹漆之。

translations.literal: Hongwu 10, all had wooden spirit objects set up, lacquered in cinnabar.
translations.idiomatic: In Hongwu 10 wooden spirit objects were set up for all and lacquered in cinnabar.

sentences.zh: 祭畢，貯於庫，仍用石主埋壇中，微露其末。

translations.literal: When the sacrifice was complete, stored in the treasury; still used stone spirit objects buried in the altar, slightly exposing their tips.
translations.idiomatic: When the sacrifice was finished they were stored in the treasury; stone spirit objects were still buried in the altar, with their tips slightly exposed.

sentences.zh: 後奉祖配，其位制塗金牌座，如先聖櫝用架罩。

translations.literal: Later when offering ancestors as collateral, their seats were gilded gold tablet holders, like the casing for the First Sage using frame and cover.
translations.idiomatic: Later, when ancestors were offered as collateral, their seats were made as gilded gold tablet holders, like the case for the First Sage, which used a frame and cover.

sentences.zh: 嘉靖中，藏於寢廟。

translations.literal: During Jiajing, stored in the sleeping temple.
translations.idiomatic: During the Jiajing reign they were stored in the sleeping temple.

sentences.zh: 帝社稷神位以木，高一尺八寸，廣三寸，硃漆質金書。

translations.literal: Emperor's altars of soil and grain spirit seats of wood, one chi eight cun high, three cun wide, cinnabar lacquer with gold inscription.
translations.idiomatic: The spirit seats at the Emperor's Altars of Soil and Grain were of wood, one chi eight cun high and three cun wide, with cinnabar lacquer and gold lettering.

sentences.zh: 壇南置石龕，以藏神位。

translations.literal: South of the altar stone shrines were placed to store spirit seats.
translations.idiomatic: Stone shrines were placed south of the altar to store the spirit seats.

sentences.zh: 王府州縣社主皆用石，長二尺五寸，廣尺五寸。

translations.literal: Princely estates, prefectures, and counties all used stone for altar-of-soil spirit objects, two chi five cun long, one chi five cun wide.
translations.idiomatic: Princely estates, prefectures, and counties all used stone spirit objects for the altar of soil, two chi five cun long and one chi five cun wide.

sentences.zh: 日月壇神位，以松柏爲之。

translations.literal: Sun and moon altar spirit seats, made of pine and cypress.
translations.idiomatic: The spirit seats at the sun and moon altars were made of pine and cypress.

sentences.zh: 長二尺五寸，廣五寸，趺高五寸。

translations.literal: Two chi five cun long, five cun wide, base five cun high.
translations.idiomatic: They measured two chi five cun long and five cun wide, with a base five cun high.

sentences.zh: 硃漆金字。
