translations.literal: Cinnabar lacquer with gold characters.
translations.idiomatic: They bore cinnabar lacquer with gold lettering.

sentences.zh: 餘仿此。

translations.literal: The rest followed this model.
translations.idiomatic: All others followed this pattern.

sentences.zh: 二十一年更定，正殿上三壇，每壇登一，籩豆各十二，簠簋各二，共設酒尊六、爵九於殿東南，西向。

translations.literal: Twenty-first year revised: on main hall three altars, each altar one deng, bian and dou twelve each, fu and gui two each, altogether six wine vessels and nine jue set at southeast of hall, facing west.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-first year the arrangement was revised: the main hall held three altars, each with one deng, twelve each of bian and dou, and two each of fu and gui; six wine vessels and nine jue were set together at the southeast of the hall, facing west.

sentences.zh: 丹墀內四壇，大明、夜明各登一，籩豆十，簠簋二，酒尊三，爵三。

translations.literal: Within red courtyard four altars: Great Brightness and Night Brightness each one deng, bian and dou ten, fu and gui two, wine vessels three, jue three.
translations.idiomatic: Within the red courtyard were four altars: Great Brightness and Night Brightness each had one deng, ten bian and dou, two fu and gui, three wine vessels, and three jue.

sentences.zh: 星辰二壇，各登一，鉶二，酒盞三十，餘與大明同。

translations.literal: Stars and constellations two altars, each one deng, xing two, wine cups thirty; the rest same as Great Brightness.
translations.idiomatic: The two altars for the stars and constellations each had one deng, two xing, and thirty wine cups; the rest matched Great Brightness.

sentences.zh: 壝外二十壇，各登一，鉶二，籩豆各十，簠簋各二，酒盞十，酒尊三，爵三。

translations.literal: Outside enclosure twenty altars, each one deng, xing two, bian and dou ten each, fu and gui two each, wine cups ten, wine vessels three, jue three.
translations.idiomatic: Outside the enclosure were twenty altars, each with one deng, two xing, ten each of bian and dou, two each of fu and gui, ten wine cups, three wine vessels, and three jue.

sentences.zh: 神祇壇，鉶三，籩豆各八。

translations.literal: Spirits and earthly powers altar, xing three, bian and dou eight each.
translations.idiomatic: At the altar for spirits and earthly powers there were three xing and eight each of bian and dou.

sentences.zh: 帝王、山川、四瀆、中嶽、風雲雷雨神祇壇，酒盞各三十，餘並同嶽鎮。

translations.literal: Emperors, mountains and rivers, Four Rivers, Central Peak, wind clouds thunder rain spirits and earthly powers altars, wine cups thirty each; the rest all same as peaks and garrisons.
translations.idiomatic: At the altars for successive emperors, mountains and rivers, the Four Rivers, the Central Peak, and wind, clouds, thunder, and rain, there were thirty wine cups each; all other vessels matched those for the peaks and garrisons.

sentences.zh: 太廟時享。

translations.literal: Grand Ancestral Temple seasonal offerings.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Ancestral Temple: Seasonal Offerings.

sentences.zh: 洪武元年定，每廟登一，鉶三，籩豆各十二，簠簋各二，共酒尊三、金爵八、瓷爵十六於殿東西向。

translations.literal: Hongwu 1 fixed: each shrine one deng, xing three, bian and dou twelve each, fu and gui two each, altogether wine vessels three, gold jue eight, porcelain jue sixteen at east and west of hall.
translations.idiomatic: In Hongwu 1 it was fixed that each shrine had one deng, three xing, twelve each of bian and dou, and two each of fu and gui; three wine vessels, eight gold jue, and sixteen porcelain jue were set together at the east and west of the hall.

sentences.zh: 二十一年更定，每廟登二，鉶二。

translations.literal: Twenty-first year revised: each shrine deng two, xing two.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-first year the arrangement was revised: each shrine had two deng and two xing.

sentences.zh: 弘治時，九廟通設酒尊九，祫祭加一，金爵十七，祫祭加二，瓷爵三十四，祫祭加四。

translations.literal: During Hongzhi, nine shrines altogether wine vessels nine, joint ceremony add one; gold jue seventeen, joint ceremony add two; porcelain jue thirty-four, joint ceremony add four.
translations.idiomatic: During the Hongzhi reign the nine shrines together had nine wine vessels, with one added for the joint seasonal offering; seventeen gold jue, with two added for the joint offering; and thirty-four porcelain jue, with four added for the joint offering.

sentences.zh: 親王配享，洪武三年定，登鉶各三，籩豆各十二，簠簋各二，酒尊三，酒注二。

translations.literal: Imperial princes collateral enjoyments, Hongwu 3 fixed: deng and xing three each, bian and dou twelve each, fu and gui two each, wine vessels three, wine ewers two.
translations.idiomatic: For imperial princes offered in collateral enjoyment, Hongwu 3 fixed three each of deng and xing, twelve each of bian and dou, two each of fu and gui, three wine vessels, and two wine ewers.

sentences.zh: 二十一年更定，登鉶各一，爵各三，籩豆各十，簠簋各二，共用酒尊三於殿東。

translations.literal: Twenty-first year revised: deng and xing one each, jue three each, bian and dou ten each, fu and gui two each, jointly wine vessels three at east of hall.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-first year the arrangement was revised: one each of deng and xing, three jue each, ten each of bian and dou, and two each of fu and gui; three wine vessels were set together at the east of the hall.

sentences.zh: 功臣配享，洪武二年定，每位籩豆各二，簠簋各二。

translations.literal: Meritorious ministers collateral enjoyments, Hongwu 2 fixed: each seat bian and dou two each, fu and gui two each.
translations.idiomatic: For meritorious ministers offered in collateral enjoyment, Hongwu 2 fixed two each of bian and dou and two each of fu and gui for each seat.

sentences.zh: 三年增定，共用酒尊二，酒注二。

translations.literal: Third year supplement fixed: jointly wine vessels two, wine ewers two.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year the arrangement was supplemented with two wine vessels and two wine ewers set in common.

sentences.zh: 二十一年更定，十壇，每壇鉶一，籩豆各二，簠簋各一，爵三，共用酒尊於殿西。

translations.literal: Twenty-first year revised: ten altars, each altar xing one, bian and dou two each, fu and gui one each, jue three, jointly wine vessels at west of hall.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-first year the arrangement was revised: there were ten altars, each with one xing, two each of bian and dou, one each of fu and gui, and three jue; wine vessels were set in common at the west of the hall.

sentences.zh: 太社稷。

translations.literal: Great Altars of Soil and Grain.
translations.idiomatic: Great Altars of Soil and Grain.

sentences.zh: 洪武元年定，鉶三，籩豆各十，簠簋各二，配位同。

translations.literal: Hongwu 1 fixed: xing three, bian and dou ten each, fu and gui two each; collateral the same.
translations.idiomatic: In Hongwu 1 it was fixed that there were three xing, ten each of bian and dou, and two each of fu and gui; the collateral seat was the same.

sentences.zh: 正配位皆設酒尊三於壇東。

translations.literal: Main and collateral seats all set wine vessels three at east of altar.
translations.idiomatic: Three wine vessels were set at the east of the altar for both the main and collateral seats.

sentences.zh: 十一年更定，每位登一，鉶二，籩豆十二，正配位共設酒尊三，爵九。

translations.literal: Eleventh year revised: each seat deng one, xing two, bian and dou twelve, main and collateral jointly wine vessels three, jue nine.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh year the arrangement was revised: each seat had one deng, two xing, and twelve bian and dou; the main and collateral seats together had three wine vessels and nine jue.

sentences.zh: 後太祖、成祖並配時，增酒尊一，爵三。

translations.literal: Later when Grand Progenitor and Chengzu were both offered as collateral, added wine vessel one, jue three.
translations.idiomatic: Later, when Grand Progenitor Taizu and Emperor Chengzu were both offered as collateral, one wine vessel and three jue were added.

sentences.zh: 府、州、縣社稷，鉶一，籩豆四，簠簋二。

translations.literal: Prefecture, department, and county altars of soil and grain: xing one, bian and dou four, fu and gui two.
translations.idiomatic: At prefectural, departmental, and county altars of soil and grain there was one xing, four bian and dou, and two fu and gui.

sentences.zh: 朝日、夕月。

translations.literal: Morning Sun and Evening Moon.
translations.idiomatic: Morning Sun and Evening Moon.

sentences.zh: 洪武三年定，太尊、著尊、山罍各二，在壇上東南隅，北面。

translations.literal: Hongwu 3 fixed: tai zun, zhuo zun, shan lei two each, at southeast corner on altar, facing north.
translations.idiomatic: In Hongwu 3 it was fixed that two each of tai zun, zhuo zun, and shan lei were placed at the southeast corner on the altar, facing north.

sentences.zh: 象尊、壺尊、山罍各二，在壇下，籩豆各十，簠簋各二，登鉶各三。

translations.literal: Xiang zun, hu zun, shan lei two each, below altar; bian and dou ten each, fu and gui two each, deng and xing three each.
translations.idiomatic: Below the altar were two each of xiang zun, hu zun, and shan lei; ten each of bian and dou, two each of fu and gui, and three each of deng and xing.

sentences.zh: 先農，與社稷同，加登一，籩豆減二。

translations.literal: Agriculture Ancestor, same as soil and grain altars, add one deng, bian and dou reduced by two.
translations.idiomatic: For the Agriculture Ancestor, the vessels matched those at the altars of soil and grain, with one deng added and two bian and dou removed.

sentences.zh: 神祇。

translations.literal: Spirits and Earthly Powers.
translations.idiomatic: Spirits and Earthly Powers.

sentences.zh: 洪武二年定，每壇籩豆各四，簠簋登爵各一。

translations.literal: Hongwu 2 fixed: each altar bian and dou four each, fu, gui, deng, jue one each.
translations.idiomatic: In Hongwu 2 it was fixed that each altar had four each of bian and dou and one each of fu, gui, deng, and jue.

sentences.zh: 九年更定，正殿共設酒尊三，爵七，兩廡各設酒尊三，爵三，餘如舊。

translations.literal: Ninth year revised: main hall jointly wine vessels three, jue seven; both wings each wine vessels three, jue three; rest as before.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year the arrangement was revised: the main hall had three wine vessels and seven jue set in common; each wing had three wine vessels and three jue; the rest remained as before.

sentences.zh: 二十一年更定，每壇登一，鉶二，籩豆各十，簠簋各二，酒盞三十。

translations.literal: Twenty-first year revised: each altar deng one, xing two, bian and dou ten each, fu and gui two each, wine cups thirty.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-first year the arrangement was revised: each altar had one deng, two xing, ten each of bian and dou, two each of fu and gui, and thirty wine cups.

sentences.zh: 星辰，正殿中登一，鉶二。

translations.literal: Stars and constellations: main hall center deng one, xing two.
translations.idiomatic: For the stars and constellations, the center of the main hall had one deng and two xing.

sentences.zh: 餘九壇，鉶二。

translations.literal: Remaining nine altars, xing two.
translations.idiomatic: The remaining nine altars each had two xing.

sentences.zh: 每壇籩豆十，簠簋各一，酒盞三十，爵一，共設酒尊三。

translations.literal: Each altar bian and dou ten, fu and gui one each, wine cups thirty, jue one, jointly wine vessels three.
translations.idiomatic: Each altar had ten bian and dou, one each of fu and gui, thirty wine cups, and one jue; three wine vessels were set in common.

sentences.zh: 太歲諸神，籩豆各八，簠簋各二，酒尊三。

translations.literal: Grand Year Star and various spirits, bian and dou eight each, fu and gui two each, wine vessels three.
translations.idiomatic: For the Grand Year Star and the various spirits there were eight each of bian and dou, two each of fu and gui, and three wine vessels.

sentences.zh: 嶽瀆山川同。

translations.literal: Peaks, rivers, mountains and rivers the same.
translations.idiomatic: The peaks, rivers, and mountains and rivers were the same.

sentences.zh: 歷代帝王。

translations.literal: Successive Dynasties' Emperors.
translations.idiomatic: Successive Dynasties' Emperors.

sentences.zh: 洪武四年定，登一，鉶二，籩豆各八，簠簋各一，俎一，爵三，尊三。

translations.literal: Hongwu 4 fixed: deng one, xing two, bian and dou eight each, fu and gui one each, zu one, jue three, zun three.
translations.idiomatic: In Hongwu 4 it was fixed that there was one deng, two xing, eight each of bian and dou, one each of fu and gui, one zu, three jue, and three zun.

sentences.zh: 七年更定，登、鉶、簠簋各一，籩豆各十，爵各三，共設酒尊五於殿西階，酒尊三於殿東階。

translations.literal: Seventh year revised: deng, xing, fu, gui one each, bian and dou ten each, jue three each, jointly wine vessels five at west steps of hall, wine vessels three at east steps.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year the arrangement was revised: one each of deng, xing, fu, and gui; ten each of bian and dou; three jue each; five wine vessels set together at the west steps of the hall, and three at the east steps.

sentences.zh: 二十一年增定，每位鉶二，簠簋各二，五室共設酒尊三，爵四十八。

translations.literal: Twenty-first year supplemented: each seat xing two, fu and gui two each, five chambers jointly wine vessels three, jue forty-eight.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-first year the arrangement was supplemented: each seat had two xing and two each of fu and gui; the five chambers together had three wine vessels and forty-eight jue.

sentences.zh: 配位每壇籩豆各二，簠簋各一，饋盤一，每位鉶一，酒盞三。

translations.literal: Collateral each altar bian and dou two each, fu and gui one each, offering tray one, each seat xing one, wine cups three.
translations.idiomatic: At each collateral altar there were two each of bian and dou, one each of fu and gui, one offering tray, one xing per seat, and three wine cups.

sentences.zh: 三皇，籩豆各八，簠簋各二，登、鉶各二，爵三，犧尊、象尊、山罍各一。

translations.literal: Three Sovereigns: bian and dou eight each, fu and gui two each, deng and xing two each, jue three, xi zun, xiang zun, shan lei one each.
translations.idiomatic: For the Three Sovereigns there were eight each of bian and dou, two each of fu and gui, two each of deng and xing, three jue, and one each of xi zun, xiang zun, and shan lei.

sentences.zh: 配位，籩豆各四，簠簋各二，鉶一，爵三，犧尊、象尊各一。

translations.literal: Collateral: bian and dou four each, fu and gui two each, xing one, jue three, xi zun and xiang zun one each.
translations.idiomatic: For the collateral seats there were four each of bian and dou, two each of fu and gui, one xing, three jue, and one each of xi zun and xiang zun.

sentences.zh: 至聖先師。

translations.literal: Most Sage and First Teacher.
translations.idiomatic: Most Sage and First Teacher.

sentences.zh: 洪武元年定，籩豆各六，簠簋各二，登一，鉶二，犧尊、象尊、山罍各一。

translations.literal: Hongwu 1 fixed: bian and dou six each, fu and gui two each, deng one, xing two, xi zun, xiang zun, shan lei one each.
translations.idiomatic: In Hongwu 1 it was fixed that there were six each of bian and dou, two each of fu and gui, one deng, two xing, and one each of xi zun, xiang zun, and shan lei.

sentences.zh: 四配位，籩豆各四，簠簋各一，登一。

translations.literal: Four collateral seats, bian and dou four each, fu and gui one each, deng one.
translations.idiomatic: For the four collateral seats there were four each of bian and dou, one each of fu and gui, and one deng.

sentences.zh: 十哲，兩廡，籩豆二。

translations.literal: Ten Wise Ones, two wings, bian and dou two.
translations.idiomatic: For the Ten Wise Ones and the two wings there were two bian and dou.

sentences.zh: 四年更定，正位，籩豆各十，酒尊三，爵三，餘如舊。

translations.literal: Fourth year revised: main seat, bian and dou ten each, wine vessels three, jue three; rest as before.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year the arrangement was revised: for the main seat there were ten each of bian and dou, three wine vessels, and three jue; the rest remained as before.

sentences.zh: 四配，每位酒尊一，餘同正位。

translations.literal: Four collateral, each seat wine vessel one; rest same as main seat.
translations.idiomatic: For the four collateral seats, each had one wine vessel; the rest matched the main seat.

sentences.zh: 十哲，東西各爵一，每位籩豆各四，簠簋各一，鉶一，酒盞一。

translations.literal: Ten Wise Ones, east and west one jue each, each seat bian and dou four each, fu and gui one each, xing one, wine cup one.
translations.idiomatic: For the Ten Wise Ones there was one jue each on the east and west; each seat had four each of bian and dou, one each of fu and gui, one xing, and one wine cup.

sentences.zh: 兩廡，東西各十三壇，東西各爵一，每壇籩豆各四，簠簋各一，酒盞四。

translations.literal: Two wings, east and west thirteen altars each, east and west one jue each, each altar bian and dou four each, fu and gui one each, wine cups four.
translations.idiomatic: In the two wings there were thirteen altars each on the east and west, with one jue each on the east and west; each altar had four each of bian and dou, one each of fu and gui, and four wine cups.

sentences.zh: 十五年更定，正位，酒尊一，爵三，登一，鉶二，籩豆各八，簠簋各二。

translations.literal: Fifteenth year revised: main seat wine vessel one, jue three, deng one, xing two, bian and dou eight each, fu and gui two each.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifteenth year the arrangement was revised: for the main seat there was one wine vessel, three jue, one deng, two xing, eight each of bian and dou, and two each of fu and gui.

sentences.zh: 四配位，共酒尊一，各爵三，登一，鉶二，籩豆各六，簠簋各一。

translations.literal: Four collateral seats, jointly wine vessel one, each jue three, deng one, xing two, bian and dou six each, fu and gui one each.
translations.idiomatic: For the four collateral seats there was one wine vessel set in common; each had three jue, one deng, two xing, six each of bian and dou, and one each of fu and gui.

sentences.zh: 十哲，共酒尊一，東西各爵五，鉶一，籩豆各四，簠簋各一。

translations.literal: Ten Wise Ones, jointly wine vessel one, east and west five jue each, xing one, bian and dou four each, fu and gui one each.
translations.idiomatic: For the Ten Wise Ones there was one wine vessel set in common, five jue each on the east and west, one xing, four each of bian and dou, and one each of fu and gui.

sentences.zh: 東西廡，每四位爵四，籩豆各二，簠簋各一。

translations.literal: East and west wings, every four seats four jue, bian and dou two each, fu and gui one each.
translations.idiomatic: In the east and west wings, every four seats had four jue, two each of bian and dou, and one each of fu and gui.

sentences.zh: 景泰六年增兩廡籩豆各二，簠簋各一。

translations.literal: Jingtai 6 added to both wings bian and dou two each, fu and gui one each.
translations.idiomatic: In Jingtai 6 two each of bian and dou and one each of fu and gui were added to both wings.

sentences.zh: 成化十二年，增正位籩豆爲十二。

translations.literal: Chenghua 12, increased main seat bian and dou to twelve.
translations.idiomatic: In Chenghua 12 the bian and dou at the main seat were increased to twelve.

sentences.zh: 嘉靖九年，仍減爲十。

translations.literal: Jiajing 9, again reduced to ten.
translations.idiomatic: In Jiajing 9 they were again reduced to ten.

sentences.zh: 旗纛，與先農同。

translations.literal: Banners and Pennants, same as Agriculture Ancestor.
translations.idiomatic: For Banners and Pennants, the vessels matched those for the Agriculture Ancestor.

sentences.zh: 馬神，籩豆各四，簠簋、登、象尊、壺尊各一。

translations.literal: Horse Spirit, bian and dou four each, fu, gui, deng, xiang zun, hu zun one each.
translations.idiomatic: For the Horse Spirit there were four each of bian and dou and one each of fu, gui, deng, xiang zun, and hu zun.

sentences.zh: ○玉帛牲牢

translations.literal: ○ Jade, silks, and sacrificial animals
translations.idiomatic: ○ Jade, Silks, and Sacrificial Animals

sentences.zh: 玉三等：上帝，蒼璧；

translations.literal: Jade three grades: Supreme Lord, azure bi;
translations.idiomatic: Jade came in three grades: for the Supreme Lord, an azure bi;

sentences.zh: 皇地祇，黃琮；

translations.literal: Sovereign Earth Spirit, yellow cong;
translations.idiomatic: for the Sovereign Earth Spirit, a yellow cong;

sentences.zh: 太社、太稷，兩圭有邸；

translations.literal: Great Altar of Soil and Great Altar of Grain, paired gui with bases;
translations.idiomatic: for the Great Altar of Soil and Great Altar of Grain, paired gui with bases;

sentences.zh: 朝日、夕月，圭璧五寸。

translations.literal: Morning Sun and Evening Moon, gui and bi five cun.
translations.idiomatic: for the Morning Sun and Evening Moon, gui and bi of five cun.

sentences.zh: 帛五等：曰郊祀制帛，郊祀正配位用之。

translations.literal: Silks five grades: called suburban-sacrifice prescribed silk, used at suburban sacrifice main and collateral seats.
translations.idiomatic: Silks came in five grades. The first was called suburban-sacrifice prescribed silk, used at the main and collateral seats of suburban sacrifice.

sentences.zh: 上帝，蒼；

translations.literal: Supreme Lord, azure;
translations.idiomatic: For the Supreme Lord, azure;

sentences.zh: 地祇，黃；

translations.literal: Earth Spirit, yellow;
translations.idiomatic: for the Earth Spirit, yellow;

sentences.zh: 配位，白。

translations.literal: Collateral, white.
translations.idiomatic: for the collateral seat, white.

sentences.zh: 曰禮神制帛，社稷以下用之。

translations.literal: Called spirit-worship prescribed silk, used at altars of soil and grain and below.
translations.idiomatic: The second was called spirit-worship prescribed silk, used at the altars of soil and grain and below.

sentences.zh: 社稷，黑；

translations.literal: Soil and grain altars, black;
translations.idiomatic: For the altars of soil and grain, black;

sentences.zh: 大明，赤；

translations.literal: Great Brightness, red;
translations.idiomatic: for Great Brightness, red;

sentences.zh: 夜明、星辰、太歲、風雲雷雨、天下神祇俱白；

translations.literal: Night Brightness, stars and constellations, Grand Year Star, wind clouds thunder rain, all-under-heaven spirits and earthly powers all white;
translations.idiomatic: for Night Brightness, the stars and constellations, the Grand Year Star, wind, clouds, thunder, and rain, and all spirits and earthly powers throughout the realm, all white;

sentences.zh: 五星，五色；

translations.literal: Five Stars, five colors;
translations.idiomatic: for the Five Stars, the five colors;

sentences.zh: 嶽鎮、四海、陵山隨方色；

translations.literal: Peaks and guardian mountains, Four Seas, imperial tomb mountains follow each direction's color;
translations.idiomatic: for the sacred peaks, the Four Seas, and imperial tomb mountains, the color followed that of the corresponding direction;

sentences.zh: 四瀆，黑；

translations.literal: Four Waterways, black;
translations.idiomatic: for the Four Waterways, black;

sentences.zh: 先農，正配皆青；

translations.literal: First Farmer, main and collateral all green;
translations.idiomatic: for the First Farmer, both the main and collateral seats were green;

sentences.zh: 羣神，白；

translations.literal: Various spirits, white;
translations.idiomatic: for the various spirits, white;

sentences.zh: 帝王先師皆白；

translations.literal: Emperors and kings and the First Teacher all white;
translations.idiomatic: for the emperors and kings and the First Teacher, all white;

sentences.zh: 旗纛，洪武元年用黑，七年改赤，九年定黑二、白五。

translations.literal: Banner and standard spirits: Hongwu 1 used black; seventh year changed to red; ninth year fixed at two black and five white.
translations.idiomatic: For the banner and standard spirits, black was used in Hongwu 1; in the seventh year this was changed to red; in the ninth year the rule was fixed at two black and five white.

sentences.zh: 曰奉先制帛，太廟用之，每廟二。

translations.literal: Called ancestral-veneration prescribed silk, used at the Grand Ancestral Temple, two per shrine.
translations.idiomatic: The third was called ancestral-veneration prescribed silk, used at the Grand Ancestral Temple, two per shrine.

sentences.zh: 曰展親制帛，親王配享用之。

translations.literal: Called extending-kinship prescribed silk, used at princely collateral offerings.
translations.idiomatic: The fourth was called extending-kinship prescribed silk, used at the collateral offerings for imperial princes.

sentences.zh: 曰報功制帛，功臣配享用之。

translations.literal: Called reporting-merit prescribed silk, used at meritorious ministers' collateral offerings.
translations.idiomatic: The fifth was called reporting-merit prescribed silk, used at the collateral offerings for meritorious ministers.

sentences.zh: 皆白。

translations.literal: All white.
translations.idiomatic: All were white.

sentences.zh: 每位各一。

translations.literal: Each seat one each.
translations.idiomatic: Each seat received one.

sentences.zh: 惟圜丘，嘉靖九年用十二，而周天星辰則共用十，孔廟十哲、兩廡東西各一云。

translations.literal: Only at the Circular Mound, Jiajing 9 used twelve; yet the stars throughout the heavens shared ten in common; at the Confucius Temple the Ten Wise Ones and the two wings east and west each had one, it is said.
translations.idiomatic: Only at the Circular Mound did Jiajing 9 prescribe twelve; the stars throughout the heavens shared ten in all; at the Confucius Temple the Ten Wise Ones and the eastern and western wings of the two corridors each had one, it is said.

sentences.zh: 又洪武十一年，上以小祀有用楮錢者爲不經。

translations.literal: Moreover in Hongwu 11, the emperor regarded the use of paper spirit money at minor sacrifices as unorthodox.
translations.idiomatic: In Hongwu 11 the emperor also held that the use of paper spirit money at minor sacrifices was improper.

sentences.zh: 禮臣議定，在京，大祀、中祀用制帛，有篚。

translations.literal: Ritual officials deliberated and fixed: in the capital, major and medium sacrifices used prescribed silk, with baskets.
translations.idiomatic: After deliberation the ritual officials fixed the rule that in the capital major and medium sacrifices were to use prescribed silk, presented in baskets.

sentences.zh: 在外，王國府州縣亦如之。

translations.literal: Outside, princely domains, prefectures, and counties likewise followed this.
translations.idiomatic: In the provinces, princely domains, prefectures, and counties followed the same rule.

sentences.zh: 小祀惟用牲醴。

translations.literal: Minor sacrifices used only sacrificial animals and fermented libations.
translations.idiomatic: Minor sacrifices used only sacrificial animals and fermented libations.

sentences.zh: 牲牢三等：曰犢，曰羊，曰豕。

translations.literal: Sacrificial animals three grades: called calf, called sheep, called pig.
translations.idiomatic: Sacrificial animals came in three grades: calf, sheep, and pig.

sentences.zh: 色尚騂，或黝。

translations.literal: Color favored sorrel, or dusky.
translations.idiomatic: Their color was preferably sorrel, or dusky.

sentences.zh: 大祀，入滌九旬；

translations.literal: Major sacrifice, entering cleansing pen nine ten-day periods;
translations.idiomatic: For major sacrifices, animals entered the cleansing pen ninety days before the rite;

sentences.zh: 中祀，三旬；

translations.literal: Medium sacrifice, three ten-day periods;
translations.idiomatic: for medium sacrifices, thirty days;

sentences.zh: 小祀，一旬。

translations.literal: Minor sacrifice, one ten-day period.
translations.idiomatic: for minor sacrifices, ten days.

sentences.zh: 大祀前一月之朔，躬詣犧牲所視牲，每日大臣一人往視。

translations.literal: Major sacrifice, on the new moon one month before, in person proceed to the sacrificial-animal pen to inspect the victims; each day one grand minister went to inspect.
translations.idiomatic: For major sacrifices, on the new moon one month beforehand the emperor went in person to the sacrificial-animal pen to inspect the victims, and each day one grand minister was sent to inspect them.

sentences.zh: 洪武二年，帝以祭祀省牲，去神壇甚邇，於人心未安，乃定省牲之儀，去神壇二百步。

translations.literal: Hongwu 2, the emperor because sacrificial animal inspection was very close to the spirit altar, people's hearts were not at ease, then fixed the inspection rite two hundred paces from the spirit altar.
translations.idiomatic: In Hongwu 2 the emperor found that the place for inspecting sacrificial animals lay too close to the spirit altar and troubled public sentiment, so he fixed the inspection rite at two hundred paces from the altar.

sentences.zh: 七年定制，大祀，皇帝躬省牲；

translations.literal: Seventh year fixed system: major sacrifice, emperor in person inspected victims;
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year the rule was fixed: for major sacrifices the emperor inspected the victims in person;

sentences.zh: 中祀、小祀，遣官。

translations.literal: Medium and minor sacrifices, dispatch officials.
translations.idiomatic: for medium and minor sacrifices, officials were dispatched.

sentences.zh: 嘉靖十一年更定，冬、夏至，祈谷，俱祭前五日親視，後俱遣大臣。

translations.literal: Jiajing 11 revised: winter and summer solstices and prayer for grain all personally inspected five days before sacrifice; afterward all dispatched grand ministers.
translations.idiomatic: In Jiajing 11 the rule was revised: for the winter and summer solstices and the prayer for grain, the emperor personally inspected the victims five days before the sacrifice; thereafter grand ministers were always dispatched.

sentences.zh: 圜丘，蒼犢；

translations.literal: Circular Mound, azure calf;
translations.idiomatic: At the Circular Mound, an azure calf;

sentences.zh: 方丘，黃犢；

translations.literal: Square Mound, yellow calf;
translations.idiomatic: at the Square Mound, a yellow calf;

sentences.zh: 配位，各純犢。

translations.literal: Collateral seats, each a pure calf.
translations.idiomatic: for the collateral seats, each a single calf.

sentences.zh: 洪武七年，增設圜丘配位。

translations.literal: Hongwu 7, added Circular Mound collateral seats.
translations.idiomatic: In Hongwu 7 collateral seats were added at the Circular Mound.

sentences.zh: 星辰，牛一，羊豕三。

translations.literal: Stars and constellations, one ox, three sheep and pigs.
translations.idiomatic: For the stars and constellations, one ox and three sheep and pigs.

sentences.zh: 太歲，牛羊豕一。

translations.literal: Grand Year Star, one ox, sheep, and pig.
translations.idiomatic: For the Grand Year Star, one ox, one sheep, and one pig.

sentences.zh: 風雲雷雨、天下神祇，羊豕各五。

translations.literal: Wind, clouds, thunder, and rain and all-under-heaven spirits and earthly powers, five sheep and five pigs each.
translations.idiomatic: For wind, clouds, thunder, and rain and for all spirits and earthly powers throughout the realm, five sheep and five pigs each.

sentences.zh: 方丘配位，天下山川，牛一，羊豕各三。

translations.literal: Square Mound collateral seats, mountains and rivers throughout the realm, one ox, three sheep and three pigs each.
translations.idiomatic: For the collateral seats at the Square Mound and for the mountains and rivers throughout the realm, one ox, three sheep, and three pigs each.

sentences.zh: 太廟禘，正配皆太牢，祫皆太牢。

translations.literal: Grand Ancestral Temple di rite, main and collateral all grand offering; xia all grand offering.
translations.idiomatic: At the Grand Ancestral Temple di rite, both main and collateral seats received the grand offering; at the xia rite all received the grand offering.

sentences.zh: 時享每廟犢羊豕各一。

translations.literal: Seasonal offerings, each shrine one calf, sheep, and pig each.
translations.idiomatic: At seasonal offerings each shrine received one calf, one sheep, and one pig.

sentences.zh: 親王配位，洪武三年定，共牛羊豕一。

translations.literal: Princely collateral seats, Hongwu 3 fixed, together one ox, sheep, and pig.
translations.idiomatic: For princely collateral seats, fixed in Hongwu 3, there was together one ox, one sheep, and one pig.

sentences.zh: 二十一年更定，每壇犢羊豕各一。

translations.literal: Twenty-first year revised, each altar one calf, sheep, and pig each.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-first year the rule was revised: each altar received one calf, one sheep, and one pig.

sentences.zh: 功臣配位，洪武二年定，每位羊豕體各一。

translations.literal: Meritorious ministers' collateral seats, Hongwu 2 fixed, each seat one sheep and pig portion each.
translations.idiomatic: For meritorious ministers' collateral seats, fixed in Hongwu 2, each seat received one portion of sheep and one portion of pig.

sentences.zh: 二十一年更定，每壇羊豕一。

translations.literal: Twenty-first year revised, each altar one sheep and one pig.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-first year the rule was revised: each altar received one sheep and one pig.

sentences.zh: 太社稷，犢羊豕各一，配位同。

translations.literal: Great altars of soil and grain, one calf, sheep, and pig each; collateral same.
translations.idiomatic: At the Great Altars of Soil and Grain there was one calf, one sheep, and one pig each; the collateral seats were the same.

sentences.zh: 府州縣社稷，正配位，共羊一、豕一。

translations.literal: Prefecture, department, and county altars of soil and grain, main and collateral seats, together one sheep and one pig.
translations.idiomatic: At prefectural, departmental, and county altars of soil and grain, the main and collateral seats together received one sheep and one pig.

sentences.zh: 洪武七年增設，各羊一、豕一。

translations.literal: Hongwu 7 added seats, each one sheep and one pig.
translations.idiomatic: When additional seats were added in Hongwu 7, each received one sheep and one pig.

sentences.zh: 朝日、夕月，犢羊豕各一。

translations.literal: Morning Sun and Evening Moon, one calf, sheep, and pig each.
translations.idiomatic: For the Morning Sun and Evening Moon, one calf, one sheep, and one pig each.

sentences.zh: 先農與太社稷同。

translations.literal: First Farmer same as Great Altars of Soil and Grain.
translations.idiomatic: The First Farmer followed the same rule as the Great Altars of Soil and Grain.

sentences.zh: 神祇，洪武二年定，羊六、豕六。

translations.literal: Spirits and earthly powers, Hongwu 2 fixed, six sheep and six pigs.
translations.idiomatic: For spirits and earthly powers, fixed in Hongwu 2, there were six sheep and six pigs.

sentences.zh: 二十一年更定，每壇犢羊豕各一。

translations.literal: Twenty-first year revised, each altar one calf, sheep, and pig each.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-first year the rule was revised: each altar received one calf, one sheep, and one pig.

sentences.zh: 嘉靖十年，天神左，地祇右，各牲五。

translations.literal: Jiajing 10, heavenly spirits left, earthly powers right, five victims each.
translations.idiomatic: In Jiajing 10 the heavenly spirits were placed on the left and the earthly powers on the right, with five victims for each.

sentences.zh: 星辰，每壇羊一、豕一。

translations.literal: Stars and constellations, each altar one sheep and one pig.
translations.idiomatic: For the stars and constellations, each altar received one sheep and one pig.

sentences.zh: 帝王，每室犢羊豕各一。

translations.literal: Emperors and kings, each chamber one calf, sheep, and pig each.
translations.idiomatic: For the emperors and kings, each chamber received one calf, one sheep, and one pig.

sentences.zh: 配位，每壇羊豕各一。

translations.literal: Collateral seats, each altar one sheep and one pig each.
translations.idiomatic: For the collateral seats, each altar received one sheep and one pig.

sentences.zh: 先師如帝王，四配如配位，十哲東西各豕一分五，兩廡東西各豕一，後增爲三。

translations.literal: First Teacher like emperors and kings; four collateral like collateral seats; Ten Wise Ones east and west each one pig divided into five portions; two corridors east and west each one pig, later increased to three.
translations.idiomatic: The First Teacher followed the rule for emperors and kings; the four collateral seats followed that for collateral offerings; for the Ten Wise Ones, east and west each received one pig divided into five portions; for the two corridors, east and west each received one pig, later increased to three.

sentences.zh: 府州縣學先師，羊一、豕一。

translations.literal: Prefecture, department, and county school First Teacher, one sheep and one pig.
translations.idiomatic: At prefectural, departmental, and county schools the First Teacher received one sheep and one pig.

sentences.zh: 四配。

translations.literal: Four collateral.
translations.idiomatic: For the four collateral seats,

sentences.zh: 共羊一、豕一，解爲四體。

translations.literal: together one sheep and one pig, divided into four portions.
translations.idiomatic: there was together one sheep and one pig, divided into four portions.

sentences.zh: 十哲東西各豕一，解爲五體。

translations.literal: Ten Wise Ones east and west each one pig, divided into five portions.
translations.idiomatic: For the Ten Wise Ones, east and west each received one pig, divided into five portions.

sentences.zh: 兩廡豕一，解爲百八分。

translations.literal: Two corridors one pig, divided into one hundred eight portions.
translations.idiomatic: For the two corridors one pig was divided into one hundred eight portions.

sentences.zh: 旗纛，洪武九年定犢羊豕，永樂後，去犢。

translations.literal: Banner and standard spirits, Hongwu 9 fixed calf, sheep, and pig; after Yongle, removed calf.
translations.idiomatic: For the banner and standard spirits, Hongwu 9 fixed a calf, sheep, and pig; after the Yongle reign the calf was removed.

sentences.zh: 王國及衛所同。

translations.literal: Princely domains and guard posts same.
translations.idiomatic: Princely domains and guard posts followed the same rule.

sentences.zh: 五祀馬神俱用羊豕。

translations.literal: Five sacrifices and Horse Spirit all used sheep and pig.
translations.idiomatic: The five household sacrifices and the Horse Spirit all used sheep and pig.

sentences.zh: ○祝冊

translations.literal: ○ Prayer placards
translations.idiomatic: ○ Prayer Placards

sentences.zh: 南北郊，祝板長一尺一分，廣八寸，厚二分，用楸梓木。

translations.literal: Southern and northern suburbs, prayer board one chi one fen long, eight cun wide, two fen thick, using catalpa and zelkova wood.
translations.idiomatic: For the southern and northern suburbs, the prayer board was one chi one fen long, eight cun wide, and two fen thick, made of catalpa and zelkova wood.

sentences.zh: 宗廟，長一尺二寸，廣九寸，厚一，用梓木，以楮紙冒之。

translations.literal: Ancestral temple, one chi two cun long, nine cun wide, one fen thick, using zelkova wood, covered with paper mulberry paper.
translations.idiomatic: For the ancestral temple, the board was one chi two cun long, nine cun wide, and one fen thick, made of zelkova wood and covered with paper mulberry paper.

sentences.zh: 羣神帝王先師，俱有祝，文多不載。

translations.literal: Various spirits, emperors and kings, and First Teacher all had prayers; texts mostly not recorded.
translations.idiomatic: Various spirits, emperors and kings, and the First Teacher all had prayer texts, though most of the texts are not recorded here.

sentences.zh: 祝案設於西。

translations.literal: Prayer table set on the west.
translations.idiomatic: The prayer table was placed on the west.

sentences.zh: ○籩豆之實

translations.literal: ○ Fillings of bian and dou
translations.idiomatic: ○ Fillings of the Bian and Dou

sentences.zh: 凡籩豆之實，用十二者，籩實以形鹽、ＡＫ魚、棗、慄、榛、菱、芡、鹿脯、白餅、黑餅、糗餌、粉餈。

translations.literal: All fillings of bian and dou: when using twelve, bian filled with molded salt, dried fish, jujubes, chestnuts, hazelnuts, water caltrop, gorgon fruit, venison jerky, white cakes, black cakes, puffed grain cakes, and powdered rice cakes.
translations.idiomatic: For all fillings of bian and dou, when twelve were used the bian held molded salt, dried fish, jujubes, chestnuts, hazelnuts, water caltrop, gorgon fruit, venison jerky, white cakes, black cakes, puffed grain cakes, and powdered rice cakes.

sentences.zh: 豆實以韭菹、醯醢，菁菹、鹿醢、芹菹、兔醢、筍菹、魚醢、脾析、豚胉、赩食、糝食。

translations.literal: Dou filled with leek pickles and vinegar sauce, duckweed pickles and venison paste, celery pickles and rabbit paste, bamboo-shoot pickles and fish paste, spleen meat, pork belly, xi food, and san food.
translations.idiomatic: The dou held leek pickles with vinegar sauce, duckweed pickles with venison paste, celery pickles with rabbit paste, bamboo-shoot pickles with fish paste, spleen meat, pork belly, xi food, and san food.

sentences.zh: 用十者，籩則減糗餌、粉餈，豆則減赩食、糝食。

translations.literal: When using ten, bian then reduced puffed grain cakes and powdered rice cakes; dou then reduced xi food and san food.
translations.idiomatic: When ten were used, the bian omitted puffed grain cakes and powdered rice cakes, and the dou omitted xi food and san food.

sentences.zh: 用八者，籩又減白、黑餅，豆又減脾析、豚胉。

translations.literal: When using eight, bian further reduced white and black cakes; dou further reduced spleen meat and pork belly.
translations.idiomatic: When eight were used, the bian further omitted white and black cakes, and the dou further omitted spleen meat and pork belly.

sentences.zh: 用四者，籩則止實以形鹽、ＡＫ魚、棗、慄，豆則止實以芹菹、兔醢、菁菹、鹿醢。

translations.literal: When using four, bian then only filled with molded salt, dried fish, jujubes, and chestnuts; dou then only filled with celery pickles, rabbit paste, duckweed pickles, and venison paste.
translations.idiomatic: When four were used, the bian held only molded salt, dried fish, jujubes, and chestnuts, and the dou held only celery pickles with rabbit paste and duckweed pickles with venison paste.

sentences.zh: 各二者，籩實慄、鹿脯，豆實菁菹、鹿醢。

translations.literal: Two each, bian filled with chestnuts and venison jerky; dou filled with duckweed pickles and venison paste.
translations.idiomatic: When two each were used, the bian held chestnuts and venison jerky, and the dou held duckweed pickles and venison paste.

sentences.zh: 簠簋各二者，實以黍稷、稻粱。

translations.literal: Fu and gui two each, filled with proso millet and panicled millet, rice and fine millet.
translations.idiomatic: Two each of fu and gui were filled with proso millet and panicled millet, and with rice and fine millet.

sentences.zh: 各一者，實以稷粱。

translations.literal: One each, filled with panicled millet and fine millet.
translations.idiomatic: When one each was used, they were filled with panicled millet and fine millet.

sentences.zh: 登實以太羹，鉶實以和羹。

translations.literal: Deng filled with plain broth; xing filled with seasoned broth.
translations.idiomatic: The deng held plain broth, and the xing held seasoned broth.

sentences.zh: 洪武三年，禮部言：「《禮記·郊特牲》曰，『郊之祭也』，『器用陶匏』，尚質也。

translations.literal: Hongwu 3, the Ministry of Rites said: "The 《Record of Rites · Suburban Sacrifice》 says, 'When the suburban sacrifice is performed,' 'vessels use pottery and gourds,' honoring simplicity."
translations.idiomatic: In Hongwu 3 the Ministry of Rites reported: "The 《Record of Rites · Suburban Sacrifice》 states, 'In the suburban sacrifice,' 'vessels are of pottery and gourd,' honoring simplicity."

sentences.zh: 《周禮·籩人》，『凡祭祀供簠簋之實』，《疏》曰，『外祀用瓦簠』。

translations.literal: The 《Offices of Zhou · Master of Bian》 says, 'For all sacrifices supply the fillings of fu and gui'; the 《Commentary》 says, 'Outer sacrifices use earthenware fu.'
translations.idiomatic: The 《Rites of Zhou · Master of Bian》 says, 'For all sacrifices supply the fillings of fu and gui'; the commentary states, 'Outer sacrifices use earthenware fu.'

sentences.zh: 今祭祀用瓷，合古意。

translations.literal: Now sacrifices use porcelain, accord with ancient intent.
translations.idiomatic: The present use of porcelain in sacrifice accords with ancient intent.

sentences.zh: 惟盤盂之屬，與古簠璺簋登鉶異制。

translations.literal: Only plates and bowls and the like differ in form from the ancient fu, gui, deng, and xing.
translations.idiomatic: Only plates, bowls, and the like differ in form from the ancient fu, gui, deng, and xing.

sentences.zh: 今擬凡祭器皆用瓷，其式皆仿古簠簋登豆，惟籩以竹。

translations.literal: Now propose all sacrificial vessels use porcelain, their forms all imitate ancient fu, gui, deng, and dou; only bian use bamboo.
translations.idiomatic: It is now proposed that all sacrificial vessels be of porcelain, their forms modeled on the ancient fu, gui, deng, and dou, with bian alone made of bamboo.

sentences.zh: 」詔從之。

translations.literal: " An edict approved it.
translations.idiomatic: " An edict approved the proposal.

sentences.zh: 酒齊仿周制，用新舊醅，以備齊三酒。

translations.literal: Wine preparations imitate Zhou system, using new and old mash, to supply the three grades of wine.
translations.idiomatic: Wine preparations followed the Zhou system, using new and old mash to supply the three grades of wine.

sentences.zh: 其實於尊之名數，各不同。

translations.literal: Their fillings in wine vessels' names and numbers each differ.
translations.idiomatic: The vessels in which they were placed and their numbers differed for each sacrifice.

sentences.zh: ○祭祀雜議諸儀

translations.literal: ○ Various deliberated rites of sacrifice
translations.idiomatic: ○ Miscellaneous Deliberated Rites of Sacrifice

sentences.zh: 其祭祀雜議諸儀，凡版位，皇帝位，方一尺二寸，厚三寸，紅質金字。

translations.literal: Its various deliberated rites of sacrifice: for all name placards, the emperor's placard square one chi two cun, three cun thick, red ground with gold characters.
translations.idiomatic: Among the various deliberated rites of sacrifice, for all name placards the emperor's placard was a square one chi two cun across and three cun thick, with a red ground and gold characters.

sentences.zh: 皇太子位，方九寸，厚二寸，紅質青字。

translations.literal: Crown prince's placard, square nine cun, two cun thick, red ground with green characters.
translations.idiomatic: The crown prince's placard was a square nine cun across and two cun thick, with a red ground and green characters.

sentences.zh: 陪祀官位，並白質黑字。

translations.literal: Attending-sacrifice officials' placards, all white ground with black characters.
translations.idiomatic: The placards of officials attending the sacrifice were all white with black characters.

sentences.zh: 拜褥。

translations.literal: Kneeling mats.
translations.idiomatic: Kneeling Mats.

sentences.zh: 初用緋。

translations.literal: Initially used crimson.
translations.idiomatic: Crimson was used at first.

sentences.zh: 洪武三年定制，郊丘席爲表，蒲爲裏。

translations.literal: Hongwu 3 fixed system: suburban mound mats with rush matting as cover, cattail as lining.
translations.idiomatic: In Hongwu 3 the rule was fixed: for suburban altars the outer cover was rush matting and the lining was cattail.

sentences.zh: 宗廟、社稷、先農、山川，紅文綺爲表，紅木棉布爲裏。

translations.literal: Ancestral temple, altars of soil and grain, First Farmer, mountains and rivers: red patterned silk as cover, red cotton cloth as lining.
translations.idiomatic: For the ancestral temple, the altars of soil and grain, the First Farmer, and mountains and rivers, the outer cover was red patterned silk and the lining was red cotton cloth.

sentences.zh: 贊唱。

translations.literal: Ritual prompting.
translations.idiomatic: Ritual Prompting.

sentences.zh: 凡皇帝躬祀，入就位時，太常寺奏中嚴，奏外辦。

translations.literal: Whenever the emperor personally sacrificed, upon entering and taking position, the Court of Imperial Sacrifices reported inner vigil, reported outer preparations complete.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever the emperor sacrificed in person, upon entering and taking his position the Court of Imperial Sacrifices announced the inner vigil and reported that outer preparations were complete.

sentences.zh: 盥洗、升壇、飲福、受胙，各致讚辭。

translations.literal: Hand-washing, ascending the altar, drinking the blessing, receiving the sacrificial meat—each delivered eulogistic phrases.
translations.idiomatic: At hand-washing, ascending the altar, drinking the blessing, and receiving the sacrificial meat, eulogistic phrases were recited for each.

sentences.zh: 又凡祀，各設爵洗位，滌爵拭爵。

translations.literal: Moreover for all sacrifices, each set jue-washing positions, rinsing jue and wiping jue.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, at every sacrifice jue-washing stations were set up, and the jue were rinsed and wiped.

sentences.zh: 初升壇，唱再拜，及祭酒，唱賜福胙。

translations.literal: Upon first ascending the altar, chant double bow; at offering wine, chant bestow blessing and sacrificial meat.
translations.idiomatic: Upon first ascending the altar the prompt was for a double bow; at the wine offering the prompt was to bestow the blessing and sacrificial meat.

sentences.zh: 洪武七年，禮部奏其煩瀆，悉刪去。

translations.literal: Hongwu 7, the Ministry of Rites memorialized that it was tedious and irreverent, and all was deleted.
translations.idiomatic: In Hongwu 7 the Ministry of Rites reported that these practices were tedious and irreverent, and they were all abolished.

sentences.zh: 上香禮。

translations.literal: Incense-offering rite.
translations.idiomatic: Incense-Offering Rite.

sentences.zh: 明初祭祀皆行。

translations.literal: Early Ming sacrifices all performed it.
translations.idiomatic: In the early Ming all sacrifices included this rite.

sentences.zh: 洪武七年以翰林詹同言罷。

translations.literal: In Hongwu 7, on the words of Hanlin Academician Zhan Tong, it was abolished.
translations.idiomatic: In Hongwu 7 it was abolished at the recommendation of Hanlin Academician Zhan Tong.

sentences.zh: 嘉靖九年復行。

translations.literal: In Jiajing 9, it was reinstated.
translations.idiomatic: It was restored in Jiajing 9.

sentences.zh: 拜禮。

translations.literal: Bowing rite.
translations.idiomatic: Bowing Rite.

sentences.zh: 初，每節皆再拜。

translations.literal: At first, at each section all performed double bows.
translations.idiomatic: Initially, a double bow was performed at each stage of the ceremony.

sentences.zh: 洪武九年，禮臣奏：「《禮記》一獻三獻五獻七獻之文，皆不載拜禮。

translations.literal: In Hongwu 9, ritual officials memorialized: "The passages on one presentation, three presentations, five presentations, and seven presentations in the 《Record of Rites》 record none of the bowing rites.
translations.idiomatic: In Hongwu 9 ritual officials reported: "The 《Record of Rites》 passages on one, three, five, and seven presentations make no mention of bowing rites.

sentences.zh: 唐、宋郊祀，每節行禮皆再拜。

translations.literal: In Tang and Song suburban sacrifices, at each section when performing the rite all double-bowed.
translations.idiomatic: In Tang and Song suburban sacrifices, officials performed double bows at each stage.

sentences.zh: 然亞獻終獻，天子不行禮，而使臣下行之。

translations.literal: Yet for the secondary and final presentations, the Son of Heaven did not perform the rite himself but had his ministers perform it below.
translations.idiomatic: Yet for the secondary and final presentations, the emperor did not perform the rite himself but had ministers carry it out on his behalf.

sentences.zh: 今議大祀中祀，自迎神至飲福送神，宜各行再拜禮。

translations.literal: Now deliberating on great and intermediate sacrifices, from welcoming the spirit through receiving blessing and sending off the spirit, each stage ought to have its own double-bow rite.
translations.idiomatic: For great and intermediate sacrifices, they proposed that from welcoming the spirit through receiving the blessing and sending the spirit off, double bows should be performed at each stage.

sentences.zh: 」帝命節爲十二拜，迎神、飲福受胙、送神各四拜云。

translations.literal: " The emperor ordered the sections to total twelve bows—welcoming the spirit, receiving blessing and sacrificial meat, and sending off the spirit each four bows, it is said.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ordered twelve bows in all: four each for welcoming the spirit, receiving the blessing and sacrificial meat, and sending off the spirit.

sentences.zh: 登壇脫舄。

translations.literal: Ascending the altar and removing shoes.
translations.idiomatic: Removing Shoes upon Ascending the Altar.

sentences.zh: 初未行。

translations.literal: At first it was not performed.
translations.idiomatic: This practice was not initially observed.

sentences.zh: 洪武八年詔翰林院臣考定大祀登壇脫舄之禮。

translations.literal: In Hongwu 8, an edict ordered Hanlin Academy officials to investigate and fix the rite of removing shoes when ascending the altar at great sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: In Hongwu 8 an edict directed Hanlin Academy officials to research and codify the rite of removing shoes when ascending the altar at great sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 學士樂韶鳳雜考漢、魏以來朝祭儀，議於郊祀廟享前期一日，有司以席藉地，設御幕於壇東南門外，設執事官脫履之次於壇門外西階側。

translations.literal: Academician Le Shaofeng broadly investigated Han, Wei, and later court sacrifice rites, and proposed that one day before suburban sacrifice and temple enshrinement, the responsible officials should spread mats on the ground, set up the imperial pavilion southeast outside the altar gate, and set the place for attending officials to remove their shoes outside the altar gate on the west side of the steps.
translations.idiomatic: Academician Le Shaofeng surveyed Han, Wei, and later court sacrificial protocols and recommended that one day before a suburban sacrifice or temple offering, officials lay mats and erect the imperial pavilion southeast of the altar gate, with a designated area outside the west steps where attendants would remove their shoes.

sentences.zh: 祭日，大駕入幕次，脫舄升壇。

translations.literal: On the sacrificial day, the imperial procession entered the pavilion, removed shoes, and ascended the altar.
translations.idiomatic: On the day of sacrifice the imperial procession entered the pavilion, removed their shoes, and ascended the altar.

sentences.zh: 其升壇執事、導駕、贊禮、讀祝並分獻陪祀官，皆脫舄於外，以次升壇供事。

translations.literal: Those ascending the altar—the attendants, guides, ritual prompters, petition readers, together with auxiliary-offering and attendant-sacrifice officials—all removed shoes outside, then in order ascended the altar to serve.
translations.idiomatic: Attendants, guides, ritual prompters, petition readers, auxiliary-offering officials, and attendant-sacrifice officials all removed their shoes outside the altar and ascended in order to perform their duties.

sentences.zh: 協律郎、樂舞生依前跣襪就位。

translations.literal: The pitch-director and music-and-dance performers, as before, barefoot in stockings took their places.
translations.idiomatic: The pitch-director and music-and-dance performers, as before, took their places barefoot in stockings.

sentences.zh: 祭畢，降壇納舄。

translations.literal: When the sacrifice was complete, they descended the altar and put on shoes.
translations.idiomatic: When the sacrifice was finished, they descended the altar and put their shoes back on.

sentences.zh: 從之。

translations.literal: It was approved.
translations.idiomatic: The proposal was approved.

sentences.zh: 嘉靖十七年罷其禮。

translations.literal: In Jiajing 17, this rite was abolished.
translations.idiomatic: This rite was abolished in Jiajing 17.

sentences.zh: ○祭祀日期

translations.literal: ○ Sacrificial dates.
translations.idiomatic: ○ Sacrificial Dates.

sentences.zh: 欽天監選擇，太常寺預於十二月朔至奉天殿具奏。

translations.literal: The Directorate of Astronomy selects; the Court of Imperial Sacrifices in advance, on the first day of the twelfth month, reports in full at the Hall of Imperial Supremacy.
translations.idiomatic: The Directorate of Astronomy selects the dates, and the Court of Imperial Sacrifices presents a full report at the Hall of Imperial Supremacy on the first day of the twelfth month.

sentences.zh: 蓋古卜法不存，而擇干支之吉以代卜也。

translations.literal: For ancient divination methods no longer survive, and selecting auspicious heavenly stems and earthly branches substitutes for divination.
translations.idiomatic: Since the ancient methods of divination were no longer practiced, auspicious days were chosen from the sexagenary cycle in place of oracle divination.

sentences.zh: 洪武七年，命太常卿議祭祀日期，書之於版，依時以祭，著爲式。

translations.literal: In Hongwu 7, the Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices was ordered to deliberate sacrificial dates, record them on a board, sacrifice according to the season, and establish as precedent.
translations.idiomatic: In Hongwu 7 the Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices was ordered to set sacrificial dates, record them on a schedule, conduct sacrifices on those fixed dates, and establish this as standard practice.

sentences.zh: 其祭日，遣官監祭，不敬失儀者罪之。

translations.literal: On the sacrificial day, officials were dispatched to oversee the sacrifice; those disrespectful or failing in ritual were punished.
translations.idiomatic: On the day of sacrifice supervisors were appointed; anyone showing disrespect or breaching protocol was punished.

sentences.zh: ○習儀

translations.literal: ○ Ritual rehearsal.
translations.idiomatic: ○ Ritual Rehearsal.

sentences.zh: 凡祭祀，先期三日及二日，百官習儀於朝天宮。

translations.literal: For all sacrifices, three and two days beforehand, all officials rehearsed the rite at the Chaotian Palace.
translations.idiomatic: For all sacrifices, officials rehearsed the ceremony at the Chaotian Palace three and two days in advance.

sentences.zh: 嘉靖九年更定，郊祀冬至，習儀於先期之七日及六日。

translations.literal: In Jiajing 9, revised: for winter solstice suburban sacrifice, rehearsal on the seventh and sixth days beforehand.
translations.idiomatic: In Jiajing 9 the schedule was revised so that for the winter solstice suburban sacrifice, rehearsals were held seven and six days in advance.

sentences.zh: ○齋戒

translations.literal: ○ Fasting and purification.
translations.idiomatic: ○ Fasting and Purification.

sentences.zh: 洪武二年，學士硃升等奉敕撰齋戒文曰：「戒者，禁止其外；

translations.literal: In Hongwu 2, Academicians Zhu Sheng and others received an order to compose a fasting-and-purification text, saying: "Jie means forbidding what is external;
translations.idiomatic: In Hongwu 2, at imperial command, Academicians Zhu Sheng and others drafted a text on fasting and purification: "Purification (jie) means restraining one's outward conduct;

sentences.zh: 齋者，整齊其內。

translations.literal: Zhai means ordering what is internal.
translations.idiomatic: Fasting (zhai) means ordering one's inward disposition.

sentences.zh: 沐浴更衣，出宿外舍，不飲酒，不茹葷，不問疾，不弔喪，不聽樂，不理刑名，此則戒也；

translations.literal: Bathing and changing clothes, lodging outside, not drinking wine, not eating meat, not inquiring after illness, not mourning the dead, not listening to music, not attending to criminal cases—this is jie;
translations.idiomatic: One bathes and changes clothes, lodges outside the palace, abstains from wine and meat, avoids inquiring after the sick, attending funerals, listening to music, and handling legal matters—this is purification (jie);

sentences.zh: 專一其心，嚴畏謹慎，苟有所思，即思所祭之神，如在其上，如在其左右，精白一誠，無須臾間，此則齋也。

translations.literal: Single-minded in the heart, stern in awe and cautious—if one has a thought, immediately think of the spirit being sacrificed to, as if above one, as if at one's left and right; pure and single in sincerity, without a moment's lapse—this is zhai.
translations.idiomatic: One focuses the mind, maintains reverent caution, and whenever a thought arises, turns it to the deity being worshipped—as though the spirit were above and beside one—maintaining pure sincerity without interruption; this is fasting (zhai).

sentences.zh: 大祀七日，前四日戒，後三日齋。

translations.literal: For great sacrifices seven days—in the first four days jie, in the last three days zhai.
translations.idiomatic: For great sacrifices the period was seven days: four days of purification followed by three days of fasting.

sentences.zh: 」太祖曰： 「凡祭祀天地、社稷、宗廟、山川等神，爲天下祈福，宜下令百官齋戒。

translations.literal: " The Taizu said: "For all sacrifices to Heaven and Earth, soil and grain, ancestral temple, mountains and rivers, and other spirits—seeking blessings for the realm—it is fitting to order all officials to fast and purify themselves.
translations.idiomatic: The Taizu said: "When sacrificing to Heaven and Earth, the altars of soil and grain, the ancestral temple, mountains, rivers, and other deities to seek blessings for the realm, all officials should be ordered to undertake fasting and purification.

sentences.zh: 若自有所禱於天地百神，不關民事者，不下令。

translations.literal: If he himself had a personal prayer to the myriad spirits of Heaven and Earth unrelated to public affairs, no order was issued.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor prayed privately to the spirits for matters unrelated to public affairs, no such order was issued.

sentences.zh: 」又曰：「致齋以五日七日，爲期太久，人心易怠。

translations.literal: " He also said: "Performing zhai for five or seven days—the period is too long, and people's minds easily grow slack.
translations.idiomatic: He added: "A five- or seven-day period of fasting is too long; minds grow slack.

sentences.zh: 止臨祭，齋戒三日，務致精專，庶可格神明。

translations.literal: Restrict to just before the sacrifice—fast and purify for three days, striving for utmost purity and concentration, so that perhaps the spirits may be reached."
translations.idiomatic: Fasting and purification should be limited to three days just before the sacrifice, pursued with utmost concentration, so that the spirits may be duly moved."

sentences.zh: 」遂著爲令。

translations.literal: " This was then established as a statute.
translations.idiomatic: This was then enacted as law.

sentences.zh: 是年從禮部尚書崔亮奏，大祀前七日，部祀官詣中書省受誓戒。

translations.literal: That year, following the memorial of Minister of Rites Cui Liang, seven days before a great sacrifice, the ministry sacrifice officials went to the Secretariat to receive sworn fasting injunctions.
translations.idiomatic: That same year, at the recommendation of Minister of Rites Cui Liang, seven days before a great sacrifice ministry officials went to the Secretariat to receive sworn injunctions on fasting.

sentences.zh: 各揚其職，不共其事，國有常刑。

translations.literal: Each performing his own duty, not sharing another's task—the state has fixed punishments.
translations.idiomatic: Each must fulfill his own office and not usurp another's duties, on pain of statutory punishment.

sentences.zh: 宗廟社稷，致齋三日，不誓戒。

translations.literal: Ancestral temple and altars of soil and grain—three days of zhai, without sworn injunction.
translations.idiomatic: For the ancestral temple and altars of soil and grain, three days of fasting were required but no sworn injunction ceremony.

sentences.zh: 三年，諭禮部尚書陶凱曰：「人心操舍無常，必有所警，而後無所放。

translations.literal: In year 3, he instructed Minister of Rites Tao Kai, saying: "Human minds in grasping and releasing are inconstant; there must be some warning, and only then will there be no laxity.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year he told Minister of Rites Tao Kai: "The human mind is inconstant; only when given a warning will it not grow careless.

sentences.zh: 」乃命禮部鑄銅人一，高尺有五寸，手執牙簡，大祀則書致齋三日，中祀則書致齋二日於簡上，太常司進置齋所。

translations.literal: " He then ordered the Ministry of Rites to cast one bronze figure, one foot five inches tall, holding an ivory tally in hand; for great sacrifices it wrote "perform zhai three days," for intermediate sacrifices "perform zhai two days" on the tally, and the Court of Imperial Sacrifices presented it and placed it at the fasting lodge.
translations.idiomatic: He then ordered the Ministry of Rites to cast a bronze figure one foot five inches tall holding an ivory tally inscribed with "fast three days" for great sacrifices or "fast two days" for intermediate sacrifices, which the Court of Imperial Sacrifices placed at the fasting lodge.

sentences.zh: 四年，定天子親祀齋五日，遣官代祀齋三日，降香齋一日。

translations.literal: In year 4, fixed: when the Son of Heaven personally sacrificed, five days of fasting; when dispatching officials to substitute, three days; when bestowing incense, one day.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year it was fixed that the emperor fasted five days when sacrificing in person, three days when dispatching an official in his place, and one day when bestowing incense.

sentences.zh: 五年，命諸司各置木牌，以警褻慢，刻文其上曰：「國有常憲，神有鑑焉。

translations.literal: In year 5, ordered each office to set up wooden placards as warnings against irreverence, with text carved on them saying: "The state has fixed statutes; the spirits have their scrutiny.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year each office was ordered to display wooden placards warning against irreverence, inscribed: "The state has fixed laws; the spirits are watching.

sentences.zh: 」凡祭祀，則設之。

translations.literal: " For all sacrifices, they were set up.
translations.idiomatic: These were displayed at every sacrifice.

sentences.zh: 又從陶凱奏，凡親祀，皇太子宮中居守，親王戎服侍從。

translations.literal: Again following Tao Kai's memorial—for all personal sacrifices, the crown prince remained at the palace to keep guard; princes in military dress attended in service.
translations.idiomatic: At Tao Kai's recommendation, whenever the emperor sacrificed in person, the crown prince remained in the palace while princes in military dress attended in escort.

sentences.zh: 皇太子親王雖不陪祀，一體齋戒。

translations.literal: Crown prince and princes, though not attending the sacrifice, alike fasted and purified.
translations.idiomatic: Though the crown prince and princes did not join the sacrifice itself, they observed the same fasting and purification.

sentences.zh: 六年，建陪祀官齋房於北郊齋宮之西南，後定齋戒禮儀。

translations.literal: In year 6, built fasting lodges for attendant-sacrifice officials southwest of the northern suburb fasting palace; later the fasting-and-purification ritual protocols were fixed.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year fasting lodges for attendant-sacrifice officials were built southwest of the northern suburb fasting palace; the full protocols for fasting and purification were later codified.

sentences.zh: 凡祭天地，正祭前五日午後，沐浴更衣，處外室，次早，百官於奉天門觀誓戒牌。

translations.literal: For sacrificing to Heaven and Earth, five afternoons before the main sacrifice, bathing and changing clothes, lodging in an outer room; the next morning, all officials at the Fengtian Gate viewed the sworn-fasting placard.
translations.idiomatic: For sacrifices to Heaven and Earth, five days before the main rite officials bathed, changed clothes, and lodged in outer quarters; the next morning all officials viewed the sworn-fasting placard at the Fengtian Gate.

sentences.zh: 次日，告仁祖廟，退處齋宮，致齋三日。

translations.literal: The next day, reported to the temple of the Ren ancestor, retired to the fasting palace, and performed zhai three days.
translations.idiomatic: The following day they notified the temple of Emperor Renzu, retired to the fasting palace, and fasted for three days.

sentences.zh: 享宗廟，正祭前四日午後，沐浴更衣，處外室。

translations.literal: For enshrining at the ancestral temple, four afternoons before the main sacrifice, bathing and changing clothes, lodging in an outer room.
translations.idiomatic: For ancestral temple offerings, four days before the main rite officials bathed, changed clothes, and lodged in outer quarters.

sentences.zh: 次日爲始，致齋三日。

translations.literal: From the next day onward, zhai three days.
translations.idiomatic: Beginning the next day, they fasted for three days.

sentences.zh: 祭社稷、朝日、夕月、周天星辰、太歲、風雲雷雨、嶽鎮海瀆、山川等神，致齋二日，如前儀。

translations.literal: For sacrificing to altars of soil and grain, Court of the Sun, Court of the Moon, all heavenly stars, Grand Year, wind clouds thunder rain, peak-and-garrison spirits of mountains and seas, mountains and rivers and other spirits—zhai two days, as in the previous protocol.
translations.idiomatic: For sacrifices to the altars of soil and grain, the sun, moon, stars, Grand Year, wind, clouds, thunder, rain, mountain and sea deities, and rivers and mountains, fasting lasted two days according to the same protocol.

sentences.zh: 凡傳制降香，遣官代祀，先一日沐浴更衣，處外室。

translations.literal: For all proclamation-of-edict and incense-bestowing, dispatching officials to substitute sacrifice—one day beforehand, bathing and changing clothes, lodging in an outer room.
translations.idiomatic: When an edict was promulgated and incense bestowed for a sacrifice performed by a dispatched official, the official bathed, changed clothes, and lodged in outer quarters one day in advance.

sentences.zh: 次日遣官。

translations.literal: The next day the official was dispatched.
translations.idiomatic: The official was dispatched the following day.

sentences.zh: 七年定制，凡大禮前期四日，太常卿至天下神祇壇奠告，中書丞相詣京師城隍廟發諮。

translations.literal: In year 7 custom fixed: for all great rites four days beforehand, the Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices went to the All-spirits Altar to report; the Secretariat Chancellor went to the capital's City God Temple to issue the proclamation.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year it was established that four days before a great ceremony the Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices reported at the Altar of All Spirits while the Secretariat Chancellor issued proclamations at the capital's City God Temple.

sentences.zh: 次日，皇帝詣仁祖廟請配享。

translations.literal: The next day, the emperor went to the Renzu temple to request ancillary enshrinement.
translations.idiomatic: The following day the emperor went to Emperor Renzu's temple to request his participation as associate spirit.

sentences.zh: 二十一年定制，齋戒前二日，太常司官宿於本司。

translations.literal: In year 21 custom fixed: two days before fasting and purification, Court of Imperial Sacrifices officials lodged in their own office.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-first year it was established that two days before fasting and purification, officials of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices lodged in their own offices.

sentences.zh: 次日，奏請致齋。

translations.literal: The next day, memorialized requesting zhai.
translations.idiomatic: The next day they memorialized requesting the commencement of fasting.

sentences.zh: 又次日，進銅人，傳制諭文武百官齋戒。

translations.literal: Again the next day, presented the bronze figure, proclamation-of-edict informing civil and military officials to fast and purify.
translations.idiomatic: The day after that the bronze figure was presented and an edict proclaimed ordering civil and military officials to fast and purify.

sentences.zh: 是日，禮部太常司官檄城隍神，遍請天下當祀神祇，仍於各廟焚香三日。

translations.literal: That day, Ministry of Rites and Court of Imperial Sacrifices officials dispatched notices to the City God, broadly inviting all spirits throughout the realm due for sacrifice, and at each temple burned incense for three days.
translations.idiomatic: That same day officials of the Ministry of Rites and Court of Imperial Sacrifices notified the City God and summoned all deities throughout the realm scheduled to receive sacrifice; incense was burned at each temple for three days.

sentences.zh: 二十六年，定傳制誓戒儀。

translations.literal: In year 26, fixed the proclamation-of-edict sworn-fasting protocol.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-sixth year the protocol for the proclamation of sworn fasting was established.

sentences.zh: 凡大祀前三日，百官詣闕，如大朝儀，傳制官宣制云：「某年月日，祀於某所，爾文武百官，自某日爲始，致齋三日，當敬慎之。

translations.literal: For all great sacrifices three days beforehand, all officials went to the court, as at a great audience; the proclamation official announced the edict, saying: "On such year month day, sacrifice at such place—you civil and military officials, beginning on such day, perform zhai three days; you must be reverent and careful.
translations.idiomatic: Three days before every great sacrifice, officials assembled at court as for a grand audience, and the proclamation officer announced: "On [date], a sacrifice will be held at [place]. Civil and military officials shall begin a three-day fast on [date] and must conduct themselves with reverent care.

sentences.zh: 」傳制訖，四拜，奏禮畢。

translations.literal: " When the proclamation was complete, four bows, reported the rite finished.
translations.idiomatic: When the proclamation was finished, all bowed four times and the ceremony was declared complete.

sentences.zh: 宣德七年，大祀南郊，帝御齋宮，命內官使飲酒食葷入壇唾地者，皆罪之，司禮監縱容者同罪。

translations.literal: In Xuande 7, great sacrifice at southern suburb—the emperor resided at the fasting palace, ordered that eunuchs who drank wine, ate meat, entered the altar, or spat on the ground all be punished; the Directorate of Ceremonial Enforcers who connived received the same punishment.
translations.idiomatic: During the Xuande 7 southern suburb sacrifice the emperor stayed at the fasting palace and ordered that any eunuch who drank wine, ate meat, entered the sacrificial enclosure, or spat on the ground be punished; officials of the Directorate of Ceremonial who overlooked such conduct were punished equally.

sentences.zh: 齋之日，御史檢視各官於齋次，仍行南京，一體齋戒。

translations.literal: On fasting days, censors inspected officials at the fasting lodges; the same applied in Nanjing—all alike fasted and purified.
translations.idiomatic: On fasting days censors inspected officials at their fasting quarters, and the same fasting rules applied in Nanjing.

sentences.zh: 弘治五年，鴻臚少卿李燧言：「分獻陪祭等官，借居道士房榻，貴賤雜處，且宣召不便。

translations.literal: In Hongzhi 5, Vice Commissioner of Ceremonies Li Sui said: "Auxiliary-offering and attendant-sacrifice officials and others, borrowing Daoist quarters and bedding—noble and low mixed together, and moreover summons are inconvenient.
translations.idiomatic: In Hongzhi 5, Vice Commissioner of Ceremonies Li Sui reported: "Auxiliary-offering and attendant-sacrifice officials lodge in Daoist quarters, mingling ranks indiscriminately, and imperial summons are difficult to deliver.

sentences.zh: 乞於壇所隙地，仿天壽山朝房禮制，建齋房。

translations.literal: Request at open ground at the altar site, following the Chaofang protocol of Tianshou Mountain, to build fasting lodges.
translations.idiomatic: He requested that fasting lodges be built on vacant land at the altar site, following the reception-hall model of Mount Tianshou.

sentences.zh: 」從之。

translations.literal: " It was approved.
translations.idiomatic: The request was approved.

sentences.zh: 嘉靖九年，定前期三日，帝御奉天殿，百官朝服聽誓戒。

translations.literal: In Jiajing 9, fixed three days beforehand—the emperor resided at the Hall of Imperial Supremacy, all officials in court dress listened to sworn fasting.
translations.idiomatic: In Jiajing 9 it was established that three days in advance the emperor presided at the Hall of Imperial Supremacy while officials in court dress received the sworn-fasting injunction.

sentences.zh: 萬曆四年十一月，禮部以二十三日冬至祀天，十八日當奏祭，十九日百官受誓戒。

translations.literal: In Wanli 4 eleventh month—the Ministry of Rites, with winter solstice heaven sacrifice on the twenty-third, the eighteenth was when the sacrifice should be reported, the nineteenth when all officials received sworn fasting.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month of Wanli 4 the Ministry of Rites noted that the winter solstice heaven sacrifice fell on the twenty-third, the report on the sacrifice was due on the eighteenth, and officials were to receive sworn fasting on the nineteenth.

sentences.zh: 是日，皇太后聖旦，百官宜吉服賀。

translations.literal: That day was the empress dowager's sacred birthday—all officials ought in auspicious dress to offer congratulations.
translations.idiomatic: But the nineteenth was also the empress dowager's birthday, when officials were required to wear festive dress and offer congratulations.

sentences.zh: 一日兩遇禮文，服色不同，請更奏祭、誓戒皆先一日。

translations.literal: One day encountering two ritual occasions, dress colors different—requested moving both the sacrifice report and sworn fasting one day earlier.
translations.idiomatic: Because two ceremonies on one day required different attire, they requested moving both the sacrificial report and sworn fasting one day earlier.

sentences.zh: 帝命奏祭、誓戒如舊，而以十八日行慶賀禮。

translations.literal: The emperor ordered the sacrifice report and sworn fasting as before, but on the eighteenth to perform the congratulatory rite.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ordered that the sacrificial report and sworn fasting remain on their original dates, with congratulatory rites held on the eighteenth instead.

sentences.zh: ○遣官祭祀

translations.literal: ○ Dispatching officials for sacrifice.
translations.idiomatic: ○ Dispatching Officials for Sacrifice.

sentences.zh: 洪武二十六年，定傳制特遣儀。

translations.literal: In Hongwu 26, fixed the proclamation-of-edict special-dispatch protocol.
translations.idiomatic: In Hongwu 26 the protocol for specially dispatched sacrificial missions by imperial proclamation was established.

sentences.zh: 是日，皇帝升座如常儀，百官一拜。

translations.literal: That day, the emperor ascended the throne as in the usual protocol; all officials one bow.
translations.idiomatic: On that day the emperor took the throne according to usual protocol and all officials performed one bow.

sentences.zh: 禮畢，獻官詣拜位四拜，傳制官由御前出宣制。

translations.literal: When the rite was complete, the offering official went to the bowing position and four-bowed; the proclamation official came forth from before the emperor to announce the edict.
translations.idiomatic: When the preliminary rites were finished, the offering official approached the bowing position and bowed four times; the proclamation officer then stepped forward from the imperial presence to announce the edict.

sentences.zh: 如祭孔子，則曰：「某年月日，祭先師孔子大成至聖文宣王，命卿行禮。

translations.literal: If sacrificing to Confucius, then said: "On such year month day, sacrifice to the Primordial Master Confucius, Great Completion, Utmost Sage, King of Cultural Propagation—command you to perform the rite.
translations.idiomatic: For a sacrifice to Confucius the edict ran: "On [date] a sacrifice to the Primordial Master Confucius, Great Completion and Utmost Sage, King of Cultural Propagation, is ordered; you are commanded to perform the rites.

sentences.zh: 」祭歷代帝王，則曰：「某年月日，祭先聖歷代帝王，命卿行禮。

translations.literal: " If sacrificing to successive emperors, then said: "On such year month day, sacrifice to the primordial sages, successive emperors—command you to perform the rite.
translations.idiomatic: For a sacrifice to successive emperors the edict ran: "On [date] a sacrifice to the primordial sages, the successive emperors, is ordered; you are commanded to perform the rites.

sentences.zh: 」俯伏，興，四拜，禮畢出。

translations.literal: " Prostrated, rose, four bows, rite complete and departed.
translations.idiomatic: The official prostrated, rose, bowed four times, and departed when the ceremony was complete.

sentences.zh: 其降香遣官儀，前祀一日清晨，皇帝皮弁服，升奉天殿。

translations.literal: The incense-bestowing official-dispatch protocol—one day before the sacrifice at early dawn, the emperor in pi-bian cap-dress ascended the Hall of Imperial Supremacy.
translations.idiomatic: For the protocol of bestowing incense and dispatching an official, on the morning of the day before the sacrifice the emperor in pi-bian dress ascended the Hall of Imperial Supremacy.

sentences.zh: 捧香者以香授獻官。

translations.literal: The incense-bearer gave incense to the offering official.
translations.idiomatic: The incense bearer handed the incense to the offering official.

sentences.zh: 獻官捧由中陛降中道出，至午門外，置龍亭內。

translations.literal: The offering official, holding it, descended the central steps and went out the central gate, reaching outside the Meridian Gate, and placed it inside the dragon pavilion.
translations.idiomatic: The offering official carried it down the central steps and out through the central gate to the Meridian Gate, where it was placed in the dragon pavilion.

sentences.zh: 儀仗鼓吹，導引至祭所。

translations.literal: Honor guard, musical drums and pipes, guided to the sacrifice site.
translations.idiomatic: An honor guard with drums and pipes escorted the incense to the sacrificial site.

sentences.zh: 後定祭之日，降香如常儀，中嚴以待。

translations.literal: Later fixed: on the sacrificial day, incense-bestowing as in the usual protocol; mid-watch strictness to await.
translations.idiomatic: Later it was established that on the day of sacrifice incense was bestowed according to usual protocol while mid-watch security was maintained in readiness.

sentences.zh: 獻官祭畢後命，解嚴還宮。

translations.literal: When the offering official's sacrifice was complete and order given, security relaxed and returned to palace.
translations.idiomatic: After the offering official completed the sacrifice and received dismissal, security was relaxed and the emperor returned to the palace.

sentences.zh: 嘉靖九年大祀遣官，不行飲福禮。

translations.literal: In Jiajing 9, great sacrifice with dispatched officials—did not perform the receiving-blessing rite.
translations.idiomatic: In Jiajing 9, when officials were dispatched for great sacrifices, the receiving-blessing rite was omitted.

sentences.zh: ○分獻陪祀

translations.literal: ○ Auxiliary offering and attendant sacrifice.
translations.idiomatic: ○ Auxiliary Offerings and Attendant Sacrifice.

sentences.zh: 凡分獻官，太常寺豫請旨。

translations.literal: For all auxiliary-offering officials, the Court of Imperial Sacrifices beforehand requested the imperial decision.
translations.idiomatic: Assignments for auxiliary-offering officials were submitted in advance to the Court of Imperial Sacrifices for imperial approval.

sentences.zh: 洪武七年，太祖謂學士詹同曰：「大祀，終獻方行分獻禮，未當。

translations.literal: In Hongwu 7, the Taizu said to Academician Zhan Tong: "For great sacrifice, only at the final presentation performing auxiliary-offering rites—is improper.
translations.idiomatic: In Hongwu 7 the Taizu told Academician Zhan Tong: "At great sacrifices, waiting until the final presentation to conduct auxiliary offerings is inappropriate.

sentences.zh: 」同乃與學士宋濂議以上，初獻奠玉帛將畢，分獻官即行初獻禮。

translations.literal: " Tong then with Academician Song Lian deliberated and presented it; when the initial presentation of jade and silk was nearly complete, auxiliary-offering officials immediately performed the initial presentation rite.
