translations.idiomatic: Zhan Tong and Academician Song Lian submitted a recommendation: auxiliary-offering officials should begin their initial presentations as soon as the main initial offering of jade and silk was nearly complete.

sentences.zh: 亞獻、終獻皆如之。

translations.literal: Secondary and final presentations—all likewise.
translations.idiomatic: The same applied to the secondary and final presentations.

sentences.zh: 嘉靖九年，四郊工成，帝諭太常寺曰：「大祀分獻官豫定，方可習儀。

translations.literal: In Jiajing 9, the four suburb works completed—the emperor instructed the Court of Imperial Sacrifices: "Great sacrifice auxiliary-offering officials must be fixed in advance before rehearsal can proceed.
translations.idiomatic: In Jiajing 9, when construction of the four suburban altars was completed, the emperor told the Court of Imperial Sacrifices: "Auxiliary-offering officials for great sacrifices must be designated in advance before rehearsals can begin.

sentences.zh: 」乃用大學士張璁等於大明、夜明、星辰、風雲雷雨四壇。

translations.literal: " Then used Grand Secretaries Zhang Cong and others at the four altars of Great Brightness, Night Brightness, Stars, and Wind Clouds Thunder Rain.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Secretaries Zhang Cong and others were assigned to the altars of Great Brightness, Night Brightness, Stars, and Wind, Clouds, Thunder, and Rain.

sentences.zh: 舊制，分獻用文武大臣及近侍官共二十四人，今定四人，法司官仍舊例不興。

translations.literal: Old system—auxiliary offering used civil and military grandees and close attendants, twenty-four in all; now fixed at four; judiciary officials as before did not participate.
translations.idiomatic: Under the old system twenty-four civil and military grandees and palace attendants served as auxiliary offerers; the new arrangement fixed the number at four, with judiciary officials still excluded as before.

sentences.zh: 凡陪祀，洪武四年，太常寺引《周禮》及唐制，擬用武官四品、文官五品以上，其老疾瘡疥刑餘喪過體氣者不與。

translations.literal: For all attendant sacrifice—in Hongwu 4, the Court of Imperial Sacrifices cited the 《Rites of Zhou》 and Tang system, proposing military officials of fourth rank and civil officials of fifth rank and above; those who were old, ill, had sores or scabies, were mutilated by punishment, in mourning, or had bodily odor were not included.
translations.idiomatic: In Hongwu 4 the Court of Imperial Sacrifices, citing the 《Rites of Zhou》 and Tang precedents, proposed that attendant sacrifice be limited to military officials of fourth rank and civil officials of fifth rank and above, excluding the aged, the ill, those with skin ailments, those mutilated by punishment, those in mourning, and those with offensive bodily odor.

sentences.zh: 從之。

translations.literal: It was approved.
translations.idiomatic: The proposal was approved.

sentences.zh: 後定郊祀，六科都給事中皆與陪祀，餘祭不與。

translations.literal: Later fixed—for suburban sacrifice, all six-section supervising secretaries participated in attendant sacrifice; for other sacrifices they did not.
translations.idiomatic: It was later established that all supervising secretaries of the Six Sections attended suburban sacrifices, but not other sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 又定凡南北郊，先期賜陪祀執事官明衣布，樂舞生各給新衣。

translations.literal: It was further fixed that for all southern and northern suburban sacrifices, in advance bright robes of cloth were bestowed on attendant-sacrifice and executive officials, and each music-and-dance student was given new garments.
translations.idiomatic: It was further stipulated that before every southern and northern suburban sacrifice, attendant and executive officials received bright ritual robes of cloth, and each music-and-dance student was issued new garments.

sentences.zh: 制陪祀官入壇牙牌，凡天子親祀，則佩以入。

translations.literal: Ivory tallies for attendant-sacrifice officials entering the altar were instituted; whenever the Son of Heaven personally sacrificed, they wore them to enter.
translations.idiomatic: Ivory tallies were instituted for attendant-sacrifice officials entering the altar; whenever the emperor performed the sacrifice in person, they wore them upon entry.

sentences.zh: 其制有二，圓者與祭官佩之，方者執事人佩之。

translations.literal: The institution had two forms: round ones were worn by sacrificing officials, square ones by executive personnel.
translations.idiomatic: There were two types: round tallies were worn by sacrificing officials, and square ones by executive personnel.

sentences.zh: 俱藏內府，遇祭則給，無者不得入壇。

translations.literal: All were stored in the inner palace treasury; when a sacrifice occurred they were issued, and without them one could not enter the altar.
translations.idiomatic: All were kept in the inner palace treasury and issued when a sacrifice was held; without a tally one could not enter the altar.

sentences.zh: 洪武二十九年，初祀山川諸神，流官祭服，未入流官公服。

translations.literal: In the twenty-ninth year of Hongwu, when mountains, rivers, and the various spirits were first sacrificed to, ranked officials wore sacrificial robes and unranked officials wore court dress.
translations.idiomatic: In Hongwu 29, when sacrifice to mountains, rivers, and the various spirits was first instituted, ranked officials wore sacrificial robes and officials below formal rank wore court dress.

sentences.zh: 洪武二十九年，從禮臣言，未入流官，凡祭皆用祭服，與九品同。

translations.literal: In the twenty-ninth year of Hongwu, following the memorial of the ritual officials, unranked officials for all sacrifices used sacrificial robes, the same as the ninth rank.
translations.idiomatic: In Hongwu 29, on the recommendation of the ritual officials, officials below formal rank were required to wear sacrificial robes for all sacrifices, the same as ninth-rank officials.
